    Trader at Ros dhomhain; partner of Harrow in the Company, and its sole holder from AE 21.
    • John Pike b. 22 an t-Samhain, AE 12 – d. 15 an Dàmhair, AE 64
      Clerk of the Company's post at Ros dhomhain.
      • Daniel Pike b. 30 an t-Iuchar, AE 42 – d. 10 an Lùnastal, AE 108
        A storekeeper on the northern concession.
        • Matthew Pike b. 14 an t-Samhain, AE 74 – d. 22 an t-Sultain, AE 127
          A miller of the northern concession.
          • William Pike b. 26 an Dàmhair, AE 99 – d. 19 an t-Ògmhios, SE 18
            Stayed in the north at the Severance.
            • Agnes Pike b. 22 an Gearran, AE 126 – d. 6 an Dùbhlachd, SE 59
              A Tuathaich teacher; opened the school at Doire ghlas with Moot money and without the council's leave, 14 am Faoilleach, SE 15.
            • Joseph Pike b. 8 an t-Iuchar, AE 141 – d. 25 an t-Ògmhios, SE 53
              A fisherman of Caol mhòr.
      • Ann Pike b. 10 an Dùbhlachd, AE 39 – d. 18 an t-Samhain, AE 118
        Married a farmer of the concession.
    • Sarah Pike b. 15 an t-Iuchar, AE 12 – d. 3 an Dàmhair, AE 77
      Went home to an Tìr Thall and is not recorded returning.

The Hales

The family of the first marriage in two tongues that any roll records, made at Baile dhìreach (26 an Cèitean, AE 7). The Moot's own genealogy traces its first speaker, Walter Hale, to that marriage. His great-grandson Peter Hale holds the Moot's chair in the present year (29 an Cèitean, DE 27).

  • Samuel Hale = Eilidh nic Ruairidh, net-maker of Baile dhìreach b. 27 an Giblean, LE 1,804 – d. 14 am Faoilleach, AE 37
    A human cooper; his marriage was entered in both the council's books.
    • John Hale b. 21 an Cèitean, AE 20 – d. 2 an t-Ògmhios, AE 74
      A cooper of Baile dhìreach, like his father.
      • Thomas Hale b. 13 an Giblean, AE 45 – d. 25 am Faoilleach, AE 113
        Claimed a customary cutting through his Ròdaich grandmother and lost it by Dunstan's rule, 4 am Màrt, AE 111.
        • Richard Hale b. 8 an Lùnastal, AE 74 – d. 2 an Giblean, AE 128
          A harbour hand in the north-west.
          • Walter Hale b. 31 am Faoilleach, AE 105 – d. 23 an Cèitean, SE 33
            A former harbour clerk; first speaker of the Moot at Caol mhòr, 25 an Lùnastal, SE 2.
            • David Hale b. 23 an t-Sultain, AE 135 – d. 1 an t-Sultain, SE 41
              Kept the Moot's minute-books in his father's time.
              • Frank Hale b. 20 an Dùbhlachd, SE 14 – d. 25 an Giblean, DE 13
                A fisherman of Caol mhòr; father of Peter Hale.
            • Alice Hale b. 21 am Faoilleach, AE 139 – d. 21 an Cèitean, DE 4
              Taught in one of the Moot's schools.
    • Mary Hale b. 12 an Lùnastal, AE 15 – d. 5 an t-Iuchar, AE 71
      A net-maker, like her mother.

The house of Mac Ùisdein of Cathair mhòr

A Ròdaich house of Cathair mhòr that held an overseer's post under the humans and the Sloc Mòr concession under the Crown (23 an Cèitean, SE 11). It sold the concession back piece by piece, and it was the only house of the vein to move its money out before the vein failed it (4 an t-Sultain, DE 13).

  • Ùisdean mac Ruairidh b. 20 an Giblean, AE 80 – d. 2 am Faoilleach, SE 3
    Held the house's overseer's post under the Company; the post is the house's first entry in any roll.
    • Uisdean mac Ùisdein = Beathag nic Iain b. 18 an Dàmhair, AE 116 – d. 9 an Cèitean, SE 42
      Given the Sloc Mòr on the humans' terms with the names changed; raised the market cross and the stone house at Cathair mhòr.
      • Ruairidh mac Uisdein b. 13 an t-Iuchar, AE 135 – d. 21 an Dàmhair, SE 66
        Held the house's share in his father's last years.
        • Alasdair mac Ùisdein b. 3 an t-Sultain, SE 19 – d. 11 am Faoilleach, SE 69
          Grandson of the first holder; borrowed against the house's share for the search for a second vein, 20 an Cèitean, SE 50, and sold half the share to meet the debt.
        • Mòrag nic Ruairidh b. 6 an Dùbhlachd, SE 13 – d. 20 am Màrt, DE 16
          Sister of Alasdair; kept the house's papers after the stone house was let to the Mine Board.
      • Dòmhnall mac Uisdein b. 28 an t-Samhain, AE 144 – d. 23 an t-Iuchar, SE 62
        Kept the quarry at Achadh dhomhain under the house's mark.
      • Catrìona nic Uisdein b. 24 an t-Sultain, AE 143 – d. 8 an Dàmhair, DE 13
        Married at Cathair mhòr; took no part in the concession.
    • Seonag nic Ùisdein b. 28 an t-Samhain, AE 116 – d. 5 an Giblean, SE 49
      Kept the house's quarry accounts at Achadh dhomhain.

A Gazetteer of Rodos

Every town of the island, by shire: when and by whom it was founded, its history, and what the annals record there.

Siorrachd Achadh àrsaidh

Achadh àrsaidh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 32,516

Founded 17 an t-Iuchar, FE 2,208 by the fishers of the capital's river. Known for the river quays that feed the capital.

An ancient field village on the Abhainn fhionn east of the capital, grown into one of the largest settlements on the island while keeping its village name. It is the seat of Siorrachd Achadh àrsaidh, and its river quays land the fish and grain that feed Cathair dhearg. It follows the order of Macha.

Cnoc dhubh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 11,443

Founded 20 an Giblean, FE 2,263 by custodians of the capital's south. Known for its black-hill citadel south of the capital.

Cnoc dhubh of Achadh àrsaidh is a black hill with a citadel, south-east of the capital, founded in the Holy Age. Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag lies to its west and the field of Muileann ghlas to its east. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Dùn chiar

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,550

Founded 2 an Cèitean, FE 862 by a custodian house guarding the capital's east. Known for its dusky hill fort east of the capital.

Dùn chiar is a hill fort of dusky stone east of Cathair dhearg, called a city for its rank rather than its people, who are few. Its citadel and walls were rebuilt in every age, and it has served as the eastern guard of the capital since the kings of the Holy Age. It follows the capital's order, the order of Macha, and its garrison takes part in the rites of Cathair dhearg.

  • 30 am Faoilleach, AE 68 — Cloth for the camps at Dùn chiar

Siorrachd Achadh chaol

Achadh chaol

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 14,431

Founded 27 an Gearran, VE 7,798 by field-clearing households of the east. Known for its narrow barley fields.

Achadh chaol is a large village of narrow barley fields and the seat of its province. Its grain goes to the mills of Muileann dhìreach, and the two places have kept the same bargain since the Holy Age. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

  • 27 an Gearran, VE 7,798 — Achadh chaol cleared
  • 5 an t-Sultain, FE 488 — The shepherds of Achadh chaol
  • 16 am Màrt, AE 110 — Achadh chaol goes to the pits

Àth dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,775

Founded 8 am Màrt, AE 90 by Ròdaich carters of the mining road. Known for the second regiment's garrison.

A straight ford with a citadel in the north-east, built as a waystation on the ore road in the Age of Strangers and fortified in the war before the Severance. Since the Long War it has been the station of An dàrna rèisimeid, the second regiment. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

  • 25 an Dàmhair, DE 21 — An dàrna rèisimeid raised

Baile dhearg

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,551

Founded 10 an t-Iuchar, LE 1,076 by farmers of Achadh chaol. Known for its red walls on the harbour road.

A red town in the east on the road to the harbour at Seann Toll. It keeps the Old Spirits.

Baile mhin

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,647

Founded 23 an Dàmhair, LE 1,175 by carters of the Achadh chaol road. Known for its wheelwrights on the Achadh chaol road.

Baile mhin grew where the road from Achadh chaol to the coast levels out, a stopping place for carts. It is a small town of wheelwrights and stables. Its people send their grain to the mills at Muileann dhìreach.

Cnoc ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 9,725

Founded 14 am Màrt, FE 37 by shepherds of the eastern uplands. Known for its red-hill sheepwalks and Cuan ruadh wool.

Cnoc ruadh of Achadh chaol is a hill town of the eastern uplands, a sheep town since the Holy Age. Its wool goes down to Cuan ruadh for shipping. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits.

Muileann dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,994

Founded 17 an Lùnastal, FE 1,432 by the custodian house of Achadh chaol. Known for its grain mills on the straight race.

Muileann dhìreach was raised to grind the barley of Achadh chaol, and its mill-race still runs straight as a ruled line from the stream above the town. In the Age of Strangers it ground for the camps as well as for its own people, and the tithe clerks kept a counting-room beside the wheel. A reading-house of the druid schools stands on the square, and the miller's guild and the school have shared its bell time out of mind.

Siorrachd Achadh mhòr

Achadh mhòr

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 42,136

Founded 2 an t-Samhain, VE 9,323 by field-clearing households of the warm springs. Known for the great granary fields.

Achadh mhòr is still called a field village, though it is one of the largest settlements on the island and the seat of its province. It is the granary of the east, and the shared-meal custom of the Holy Age is said to have been kept here most faithfully. Travellers on the road stop at An Sligeanach Fad' às nearby.

  • 2 an t-Samhain, VE 9,323 — Fields at Achadh mhòr
  • 28 am Faoilleach, AE 143 — Achadh mhòr keeps the ledgers
  • 22 am Màrt, DE 9 — Achadh mhòr's drovers

Ceann bhàn

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 6,325

Founded 29 an t-Samhain, LE 1,063 by the tavern-keepers of the white headland. Known for An Sligeanach Fad' às and dried venison.

A walled river port on a pale headland where the Abhainn gheal meets the Abhainn bhàn, with the famous tavern An Sligeanach Fad' às at its gate, where travellers eat dried venison. It grew around the tavern road, and its walls went up in the troubles, when the roadside houses became militia posts. It keeps the Old Spirits, trades with the great village of Achadh mhòr close by, and sends its goods down the Abhainn bhàn to Seann Warr on the coast.

Siorrachd Achadh naomh

Achadh naomh

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 26,585

Founded 5 an t-Ògmhios, VE 9,414 by settlers of the spring-fields. Known for its holy field by Colbh Cnoc chiar.

Achadh naomh is a large village and the seat of its province in the north-central country, settled in the Ancient Age beside a spring held sacred. Colbh Cnoc chiar stands to its east, carved 'remember the fire'. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits.

  • 5 an t-Ògmhios, VE 9,414 — Achadh naomh's spring-fields
  • 16 am Màrt, AE 23 — The hearths of Achadh naomh

Achadh naomh

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 24,923

Founded 28 an t-Sultain, FE 2,324 by Ròdaich households of the ancestor feasts. Known for the ancestor feasts on the unploughed field.

The holy field was a meeting ground for the ancestor feasts of the Old Spirits before any house stood on it, and the houses were built around its edge rather than upon it. It is now a village of twenty-five thousand and the seat of its province, yet the field at its heart is still left unploughed. The feasts are kept there as they were in the Holy Age.

Àth chaol

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,559

Founded 20 an t-Sultain, FE 2,379 by the ford-keepers of Achadh naomh. Known for its narrow ford on the Inis mhin road.

A narrow ford in the east where the road to the harbour at Inis mhin crosses a stream. It keeps the Old Spirits of the Ròdaich, and its ford runs low in the dry months. It is a small market town for the holy field of Achadh naomh.

Cnoc bheag

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 6,478

Founded 9 an t-Ògmhios, LE 1,100 by the herders of Achadh naomh. Known for its hilltop refuge for eastern herds.

A small walled hill in the east, raised as a refuge for the herds of Achadh naomh in the troubled years. Its pastures are thin, and the town has always kept fewer herds than its walls could shelter. It keeps the Old Spirits.

Cnoc chiar

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,269

Founded 24 an Lùnastal, FE 10 by keepers of the Colbh. Known for the stone of 'remember the fire'.

A dusky hill near the standing stone Colbh Cnoc chiar, which carries only the words Cuimhnich an teine, 'remember the fire'. The stone was old when the town was founded, and the town grew around the families who tended it. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith, whose druids still come to argue over a bidding that no one has explained.

Cuan àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 11,749

Founded 28 an Dùbhlachd, FE 2,483 by the river-lords of the Abhainn ìseal. Known for the island's oldest working jetty.

An ancient river port a little below Cuan bheag on the Abhainn ìseal, trading grain from the fields around Baile fhiadhaich since the Holy Age. The Green Death, A' Phlàigh Uaine, struck the town in the Age of Strangers. It follows the capital's order, the order of Macha. Its stone jetty is held to be the oldest on the island still in use, and it is patched each generation rather than rebuilt.

Inis mhin

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 3,620

Founded 20 an Cèitean, VE 8,495 by fowlers of the eastern cliffs. Known for its causeway harbour and seal-oil.

A smooth low island joined to the shore by a causeway, walled, with a small harbour. The fowlers who settled it in the Ancient Age became traders and then wall-builders, since the eastern waters were a haunt of pirates in the Age of Strangers. It keeps the Old Spirits and is the harbour for Àth chaol and Achadh naomh.

  • 20 an Cèitean, VE 8,495 — Inis mhin settled

Muileann dhubh

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 3,306

Founded 27 an Dùbhlachd, LE 1,019 by millers of Achadh naomh. Known for its black mill of the northern road.

The black mill stands on the northern road near Tobar ghorm, grinding for the villages of Achadh naomh province. Its wheel was darkened, the old telling says, by ore dust carried downstream from the mining roads. It is a small town and has always been one.

Siorrachd Achadh shean

Achadh shean

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 24,587

Founded 21 an Giblean, VE 8,448 by Ròdaich farming households. Known for the old fields and the Long Drought.

Achadh shean, the old field, is a village of twenty-five thousand and the seat of its province. It gave its name to Tiormachd Achadh shean, the Long Drought, which settled over the island's dry season for three years running in the Age of Strangers. Its granaries were emptied in those years and rebuilt larger afterward, and they are the largest on the eastern coast.

  • 21 an Giblean, VE 8,448 — Achadh shean resettled
  • 15 an t-Iuchar, FE 2,900 — Drought at Achadh shean
  • 2 an t-Samhain, LE 1,489 — The water-rights of Achadh shean
  • 28 an t-Ògmhios, AE 107 — The wells of Achadh shean
  • 29 an Dàmhair, AE 109 — The Mission's wells
  • 9 am Faoilleach, SE 44 — Grain by the ore line

Àth chrom

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,795

Founded 9 an Giblean, LE 264 by carters of Achadh shean. Known for its bent ford on the Achadh shean road.

A small town at a bent ford on the road from Achadh shean to the coast. It lives on the road and has never been more than a crossing.

Muileann chiar

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,080

Founded 10 an Gearran, FE 98 by keepers of the sacred forest. Known for its keepers of the sacred forest's edge.

Muileann chiar of Achadh shean stands at the edge of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar, the forest marked sacred before any faith claimed it. Its people were party to the holy-wood dispute of the Holy Age and have kept the forest's edge since. Tiormachd Achadh shean, the Long Drought, struck it in the Age of Strangers. It is not the silver town of the same name. Its smiths make arms for the east coast.

  • 7 an Dùbhlachd, FE 118 — The stag in the grove
  • 15 am Màrt, FE 914 — The stag-letters
  • 3 an Lùnastal, FE 1,255 — Tormod Scrìobhaiche learns the letters

Siorrachd Àth àrsaidh

Àth àrsaidh

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 16,434

Founded 12 an t-Samhain, VE 8,781 by quarrying households of the north-west; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the ancient ford of the Tuathaich.

An ancient ford in the north-west, the seat of Siorrachd Àth àrsaidh, resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It is a large town of the Church and the market of the Tuathaich southern country.

  • 1 an t-Sultain, VE 8,819 — Stone axes from the north
  • 13 an Giblean, VE 8,870 — The quarry at Àth àrsaidh
  • 2 an t-Samhain, AE 150 — The truce of Àth àrsaidh
  • 11 an Gearran, SE 34 — The Tuathaich doctors

Àth gheal

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 12,996

Founded 29 an t-Sultain, LE 682 by Ròdaich ferrymen; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for a walled town of the coal-holdouts.

Àth gheal was a Ròdaich ford-and-harbour town of the long quiet centuries, walled in the Age of Strangers and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. When dubhan came into use it was among the northern towns that went on working the last coal seams. It was one of the holdouts broken in An Cogadh Fada, and its people still speak bitterly of that year.

Baile gheal

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 8,925

Founded 27 an Giblean, FE 715 by Ròdaich salt-boilers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the church in the old shrine.

A white-washed Ròdaich village of the Holy Age, it was one of the settlements emptied and handed to the Tuathaich after the Severance. The newcomers made it a town and a market, trading with the harbour at Caol naomh a short distance away. Its church stands in the shell of the older Ròdaich shrine of Manannan, and the two sets of carvings can still be told apart.

Baile ghlas

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 12,477

Founded 13 an t-Samhain, LE 318 by Ròdaich green-dyers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for its green dyes and Tuathaich church feasts.

A green-grey town of dyers, emptied at the Severance and resettled by the Tuathaich. It keeps the Tuathaich Church and is a market for Baile Mòr ruadh and Cnoc ghlas.

Baile Mòr ruadh

city · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 9,642

Founded 3 an Gearran, FE 2,252 by Ròdaich lords, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the red city of the Tuathaich.

A red walled city in the north-west, held by Ròdaich lords from the Holy Age to the Severance, and since then one of the principal Tuathaich cities. It follows the faith of the Church and governs the Àth àrsaidh country with its fords and towns.

  • 20 an t-Samhain, AE 150 — Baile Mòr ruadh receives the columns

Cnoc ghlas

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 2,120

Founded 13 an Cèitean, AE 22 by human settlers from an Tìr Thall. Known for its strangers' settlement on the grey hill.

Cnoc ghlas of Àth àrsaidh was settled by humans in the Age of Strangers and became a Tuathaich town after the Severance. It keeps the faith of the Church, and its singers are among the keepers of the voyage of Naomh Breandan.

Cnoc ghlas

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 1,740

Founded 12 an Dùbhlachd, LE 1,275 by Ròdaich herders, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for its trade across the line at Muileann chrom.

A small green-grey hill town of the north-west, emptied and resettled at the Severance. It follows the faith of the Church and trades with the Ròdaich mill at Muileann chrom over the line.

Doire mhòr

village · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 13,974

Founded 24 an t-Sultain, FE 1,316 by Ròdaich woodwards; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for its great oakwood and charcoal.

A great oakwood village, resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance and now one of the largest places they hold, with fourteen thousand people. It lives on timber and charcoal, and its charcoal fed the northern smithies when the ore was no longer theirs to burn. It follows the faith of the Church.

Siorrachd Àth bheag

Àth bheag

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 20,251

Founded 26 an Cèitean, VE 9,670 by Ròdaich ford-keepers of the east coast. Known for its east-coast ford under pirate watch.

Àth bheag is a town of twenty thousand at a ford of the Abhainn dhubh on the east coast, the seat of its province. Pirate ships have been seen offshore, and the town keeps watchers on the dunes. The lighthouse of Baile ìseal lies a short way south. Its salt-pans supply the whole eastern seaboard.

  • 26 an Cèitean, VE 9,670 — Àth bheag on the eastern coast
  • 26 an Cèitean, SE 32 — Salt-pans of Àth bheag
  • 9 am Faoilleach, SE 45 — The pirates' names
  • 11 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8 — The eastern salt-road

Baile ìseal

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,763

Founded 14 an t-Samhain, LE 197 by fishers of the far east coast. Known for Taigh-solais Baile ìseal and the pirate watch.

A small low town on the far east coast, beside Taigh-solais Baile ìseal, one of the five lighthouses completed in the Age of Strangers. Pirates are still seen off this coast, and the keepers of the light are also the town's watch. It keeps the Old Spirits.

  • 9 an Cèitean, AE 28 — The keepers of Baile ìseal

Siorrachd Àth chiar

Àth chiar

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 18,876

Founded 18 an Giblean, FE 2,769 by the drovers of the south-east. Known for the rebels' keep and southern cattle-market.

A dusky ford in the south-east with a citadel, the seat of Siorrachd Àth chiar and a large market town. Its keep was held by Ròdaich rebels in the war before the Severance and is still garrisoned. It keeps the Old Spirits and trades with the coast at Seann Mhorn and Muileann chiar to the south.

  • 26 an Cèitean, FE 2,875 — The flood at Àth chiar
  • 29 am Faoilleach, LE 484 — The drovers of Àth chiar

Seann Mhorn

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,960

Founded 31 an Cèitean, VE 1,814 by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for its small old harbour.

Seann Mhorn is a small old harbour, one of several Seann names on this stretch of the southern coast, and was settled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age. It lies between Seann Skell and Seann Vell. It is a fishing village of three thousand.

  • 4 an Cèitean, VE 2,046 — The shell beds of the southern Seann Mhorn

Seann Warr

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 3,337

Founded 15 an Gearran, VE 2,245 by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for its old landing on the gulf's south shore.

Seann Warr of Àth chiar is a small harbour on a Seann-Dhaoine landing on the south shore of the gulf. The Ròdaich resettled it in the Holy Age. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits and a few boats, and pays its dues to the larger harbours across the water.

  • 3 an t-Ògmhios, VE 5,712 — The tally wall of Seann Warr
  • 6 an Giblean, VE 5,793 — The bad years in the counts
  • 4 an t-Iuchar, AE 150 — Grain from Seann Warr

Siorrachd Àth dhomhain

Àth dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 17,119

Founded 19 an Lùnastal, LE 1,611 by Raghnall Àthach and his kin. Known for the horseman's ford and shire citadel.

The deep ford here could only be crossed on horseback, and a family of ferrymen became a family of lords by owning the one safe path over it. The citadel on the near bank was fought for in the troubles before the Severance and has been the seat of Siorrachd Àth dhomhain since. The town is large and orderly, a house of the druid schools stands by the gate, and Cnoc mhòr and Baile gheal send it their grain.

  • 27 am Màrt, AE 143 — The northern pits at Àth dhomhain

Baile ghorm

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 5,197

Founded 7 am Màrt, LE 1,757 by slate-quarriers of Àth dhomhain. Known for its blue slate quarries.

Baile ghorm is a quarry town whose blue slate roofs half the northern plain. It sends slate to Inis mhòr and takes grain in return. It shares its name with a dyers' town far to the east, and the two are told apart by their provinces.

Cnoc mhòr

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,757

Founded 11 an Dùbhlachd, FE 2,375 by hill-farmers of the Àth dhomhain country. Known for its hill farms and its quarrel with Baile gheal.

The great hill above Baile gheal, farmed since the Holy Age and never walled, since Baile gheal's walls stand close below. The two towns share a market and a long quarrel over which is the elder. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Siorrachd Àth fhiadhaich

Àth fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 19,293

Founded 13 an Dùbhlachd, VE 9,648 by Ròdaich herders of the wild cattle. Known for its wild ford of the eastern road.

Àth fhiadhaich stands in the south-eastern hills at the ford where the eastern road crosses the meeting of the Abhainn gheal and the Abhainn bhàn, and it has been a river landing since the Holy Age. The traffic of the vein country made it great in the Age of Strangers, and the far-famed road-house An Sligeanach Fad' às stands at Ceann bhàn, a short way down the road. The town keeps the Old Spirits, the oldest folk rite, and its river fishers still bless their nets at the ford. Copper is mined in the hills behind it, and the town's new street is named for the Sloc Mòr.

Àth fhionn

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 15,519

Founded 26 an Giblean, FE 900 by drovers of the southern roads. Known for its fording place of the southern drove road.

Àth fhionn, the fair ford, is a large inland town at the crossing of the southern drove road. It has been a resting place for herds and drovers since the Holy Age. Its people keep the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits and hold the drove-road fair at the ford.

  • 16 an t-Iuchar, VE 2,636 — The kerbed way between the forts

Siorrachd Àth ghlas

Àth ghlas

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 17,813

Founded 12 an t-Iuchar, FE 373 by Ròdaich ford-keepers of the central country. Known for its grey ford below the ruined outpost.

The grey ford is the seat of its province, a large town beside Cathair mhòr and a short way from the ruin of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire. The ruin is older than any other dwelling-place known on the island, and the town has kept its people out of it by custom. It lives on trade between Cathair mhòr and the eastern towns.

Doire bhàn

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,837

Founded 7 an t-Sultain, LE 1,287 by Ròdaich woodwards of Àth ghlas. Known for its white-barked copse by Àth ghlas.

A small village in a copse of white-barked trees across the river from Àth ghlas, cutting firewood and poles for the town. It keeps clear of the ruin of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire to the east, as its elder neighbour does. It follows the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Siorrachd Àth mhòr

Àth mhòr

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 12,234

Founded 1 an t-Ògmhios, VE 7,170 by households of the northern ford. Known for its walled great ford of the north.

Àth mhòr is the walled great ford of the north and the seat of its province, a town of twelve thousand. Its walls were raised in the Age of Strangers, when the northern road carried ore to the coast and the ford was worth holding. Baile bheag lies across the river and handles the traffic after the gates are shut.

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,961

Founded 20 an Dùbhlachd, LE 180 by carters across the ford from Àth mhòr. Known for its carters at the ford.

A small town across the ford from Àth mhòr, grown up to serve the traffic that the walled town would not let in after dark. It is a town of stables, carters and cheap lodging. It has always hung on Àth mhòr and has never been allowed a market of its own.

Siorrachd Àth shean

Àth chiar

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 9,862

Founded 21 an Dùbhlachd, LE 1,362 by ford-keepers of the east road. Known for its dusky ford near Muileann ghlas field.

Àth chiar is a ford town east of the capital, founded in the long quiet centuries. The field of Muileann ghlas lies to its south-west, and the town was a supply post in the last battle of An Cogadh Fada. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha. The ford carries Rathad na Mèinne, the ore road from the capital to the hills.

Àth shean

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 23,705

Founded 9 an t-Iuchar, VE 7,684 by farming households of the ford. Known for its old ford of the eastern road.

The northern of the two Àth shean holds the old ford where the road east from the capital crosses its river. It was walled in the Holy Age to guard that crossing and has grown into a large town. An Taigh-seinnse Mòr stands a short way up the road toward Seann Vell. The dark wine pressed on its slopes is sold along the eastern road.

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 37,915

Founded 15 an Dàmhair, FE 1,963 by ford-wardens of the south. Known for the great southern ford market.

The southern Àth shean is the larger of the two, a great ford town near the south coast. It has been a market since the Holy Age and has never needed walls. Its harbour is the old site of Seann Chwen, a short way east.

Baile uaine

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,857

Founded 5 an Gearran, LE 1,132 by market gardeners of Àth shean. Known for its market gardens for the capital.

Baile uaine is a small town of market gardens, sending green stuff to Dùn gheal and on to the capital each market day. It has never been walled or fought over. Its people follow the capital's order, the order of Macha, and pay their dues at Dùn gheal.

Cnoc òg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,778

Founded 24 an Cèitean, LE 124 by farmers from Àth shean. Known for its lodgings for the Fèill Muileann òg.

A young hill town close to Muileann òg, whose fair is the largest gathering on the island. It lodges traders and their beasts during the fair and is quiet the rest of the year. It follows the order of Macha.

Cnoc òg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,925

Founded 17 an t-Sultain, AE 43 by suppliers to the garrison at Inis mhòr. Known for its supplies for the first regiment.

Cnoc òg grew up in the Age of Strangers to supply the garrison at Inis mhòr, where the first regiment is now stationed. It is a town of bakers and harness-makers. It follows the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Dùn gheal

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,211

Founded 26 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,934 by a custodian house of the southern approach. Known for its white-limed hill fort.

The white fort is ranked a city though it holds only a few thousand people, a hill fort limed white so that it could be seen from the capital. It watched the southern road in the Holy Age and has done so since. It is now the market for Baile uaine and the farms of Àth shean.

Seann Chwen

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,732

Founded 29 an Lùnastal, VE 3,488 by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for its south-coast old harbour.

Seann Chwen of Àth shean is a harbour on the south coast, on a Seann-Dhaoine site. It was resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age and is the port for the southern Àth shean. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha.

  • 5 an Cèitean, VE 5,833 — The half-cut stone of Seann Chwen

Siorrachd Baile àrsaidh

Baile àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 20,073

Founded 19 an t-Samhain, FE 879 by settlers from Cathair dhomhain. Known for the school of Manannan's druids.

Baile àrsaidh is the ancient town of the west, the seat of its province and the place where the druids of the order of Manannan have kept their school since the orders divided. It is a large town of twenty thousand. It trades with Seann Skell to the north and with the fleet at Cuan shean to the south.

Doire chaol

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 5,858

Founded 16 an t-Ògmhios, LE 123 by Ròdaich woodwards of Baile àrsaidh. Known for its narrow oakwood of Baile àrsaidh.

A village in a narrow oakwood south of Baile àrsaidh, felling for the yards at Cuan shean as the larger Doire gharbh does. The two oakwood villages have argued over the same buyers in every age. It follows the order of Manannan.

Seann Bhral

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 20,300

Founded 5 an Dàmhair, VE 79 by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for its west-coast harbour of the order of Manannan.

Seann Bhral of the west coast is a Seann-Dhaoine site the Ròdaich resettled in the Holy Age. It grew into a large port on the western sea roads and took up the order of Manannan, the Old Faith's order of the sea, which is strong along this coast. Its harbour is unwalled, trusting to the citadel at Ros bheag to the north.

Siorrachd Baile chaol

Àth dhearg

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 4,282

Founded 25 am Faoilleach, FE 1,464 by Ròdaich keepers of the holy wood. Known for its ford at the edge of the holy wood.

Àth dhearg stands at the edge of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar, and its people have acted as keepers of the wood's western paths since the Holy Age. Walls were raised in the Age of Strangers to keep timber-cutters out of the forest as much as to keep raiders out of the town. It is not the Àth dhearg of the lighthouse in the north.

Àth mhòr

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 13,331

Founded 12 an t-Samhain, FE 2,418 by Ròdaich road-keepers of Baile chaol. Known for the great ford and the temple-ruin path.

The great ford carries the road from Seann Dunn inland, and for most of its history it has been the busiest crossing in the province. A path leaves the town southward to Làrach an Teampaill, and the folk of Àth mhòr have kept that path cleared for as long as there are accounts of it, though they will not say why. It is a large, plain town of carters, smiths and innkeepers.

Baile chaol

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 17,907

Founded 30 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,339 by the valley-folk of the eastern narrows. Known for its terraced houses and the valley toll.

A town squeezed into a narrow valley in the east and the seat of Siorrachd Baile chaol. Its houses climb the valley sides in rows, and the one road through it has been tolled since the Holy Age. It keeps the Old Spirits and trades with the city of Baile Mòr dhìreach and the market at Cnoc uaine; the sacred forest of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar lies on its western edge.

Baile Mòr dhìreach

city · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 11,777

Founded 7 an Gearran, FE 2,051 by custodians of the eastern road. Known for its citadel on the eastern road.

Baile Mòr dhìreach of Baile chaol is a citadel city on the eastern straight road, founded in the Holy Age to hold the road between the vein country and the coast. It was a tithe station in the Age of Strangers, and the ledgers kept there were among those burned in the raids before the Severance. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits and is the market town of the east coast. The first glass-house on Rodos was built here and still works, and the town also makes cheese, boots and sail-cloth.

Cnoc uaine

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 16,670

Founded 21 an Cèitean, FE 2,852 by Ròdaich keepers of the holy wood. Known for its green hill on the holy wood's edge.

Cnoc uaine is a green hill on the Abhainn mhin at the edge of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar. It is a large town of nearly seventeen thousand, and its people share the keeping of the wood with Àth dhearg. It keeps the Old Spirits, though the wood itself is sacred to Flidais and held by the druid schools.

Seann Dunn

city · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 8,890

Founded 22 an Dùbhlachd, VE 130 by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for its Seann-Dhaoine harbour stones and its citadel.

The harbour stones of Seann Dunn are older than any Ròdaich work, and the name the Ròdaich gave the place keeps a root that is not their own. It became a Ròdaich port in the Holy Age, and its citadel was raised above the harbour to guard the eastern approaches. It is now a city of shipping and salt-fish, and its oldest families still claim that the harbour wall was only repaired, never built, by their ancestors. Its yards build seagoing hulls and cut their sails.

Achadh fhada

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,735

Founded 30 an Dùbhlachd, LE 916 by barley-farmers of the south-west. Known for its long field of barley.

Achadh fhada, the long field, is a village of barley farms in the capital's southern country. It was founded in the long quiet centuries and has changed little since. It keeps the order of the Stone, unlike most of its neighbours.

Baile àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 12,323

Founded 1 an Gearran, FE 476 by custodians of the capital's south. Known for its old citadel of the southern country.

Baile àrsaidh, the ancient town, is a citadel town of the capital's southern country, founded in the Holy Age. Its citadel guards the market at Baile chiar. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Baile chiar

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 23,760

Founded 1 an Gearran, FE 869 by farmers of the capital's southern country. Known for its market of the capital's southern country.

Baile chiar, the dusky town, is the market and provincial seat of the capital's southern country. It has been a farm market since the Holy Age and has never been walled; the citadel at Baile àrsaidh stands close by. Grain from Achadh fhada and the southern farms comes to its market. Its chartered weavers make cloth from southern wool.

Cill chiar

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,848

Founded 16 an Dùbhlachd, LE 1,283 by druids of Macha. Known for the temple-house watching the unclaimed forest.

A small temple-site village at the edge of Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag, the forest no one has settled or wholly charted. Its temple-house was built to watch the forest rather than enter it. It follows the order of Macha.

Cnoc ìseal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,835

Founded 4 an Dàmhair, LE 870 by the garrison of the capital's south road. Known for its walled hill on the capital's south road.

Cnoc ìseal of Baile chiar is a walled hill on the capital's south road, founded in the long quiet centuries as a watch-post over the southern farms. Its walls were strengthened in the war of the Severance. It is a small town now. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha, and a toll it no longer collects.

Siorrachd Baile chrom

Baile chrom

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 27,319

Founded 2 an Dùbhlachd, VE 7,787 by households from Cnoc ghorm; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the Grey Night vigil and the lighthouse.

A bent town on the far north-west coast, the seat of Siorrachd Baile chrom, beside Taigh-solais Baile chrom, the first of the five lighthouses as the ring is counted round the coast to Tobar dhearg. Since the Severance it has been Tuathaich, and it is the one town where Rùn-dìomhair na h-Oidhche Glaise, the Church's vigil of the Grey Night, holds the majority; its one night of silence is kept for an Gèadh Fiadhaich, the wild goose of the Holy Spirit. Gorta Baile chrom, the Great Hunger, takes its name from this town, which it struck in the Age of Strangers. Manannan's priests at Ceann mhòr hold that the Grey Night grew out of their own harbour prayer to keep the sea shut, and call it their prayer gone astray; the Church's bishops call it irregular.

A small ford in the west on the road between Baile fhiadhaich and Cnoc ìseal. It follows the order of Manannan and has never been much more than a crossing, though crown regiments marched through it to Àth leathan in the Long War.

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 25,789

Founded 17 an t-Iuchar, VE 8,032 by settlers of the western coast. Known for its west-coast market harbour.

Baile fhiadhaich of the west is a large harbour town and the seat of its province, settled in the Ancient Age. It lies near the field of Àth leathan, and its people remember the first battle of An Cogadh Fada. It keeps the order of Manannan.

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,367

Founded 18 an Gearran, LE 1,599 by millers of the west. Known for its smooth-stone mill of the west.

Muileann mhin of Baile fhiadhaich is a mill town of the west, founded in the long quiet centuries on a stream that turns smooth stones. It grinds for the harbour at Baile fhiadhaich. It keeps the order of Manannan, and its millers are known for honest measures.

Achadh mhin

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,865

Founded 19 an Lùnastal, LE 1,801 by Ròdaich farmers of Baile gharbh. Known for its smooth fields of Baile gharbh.

A village of smooth, well-drained fields that feeds the harbour at Ceann dhubh. It is not the Achadh mhin of the southern coast that the Great Wave struck. It has had few recorded troubles and is mentioned in the older rolls chiefly for its tithe.

Àth fhada

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 11,371

Founded 12 an t-Sultain, FE 2,509 by ford-keepers of the north-east road. Known for its long ford of the north-east road.

Àth fhada, the long ford, is a town on the north-east road, founded in the Holy Age. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith. Its ford is long and shallow, and carts cross it only at low water.

Baile gharbh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 35,209

Founded 15 an Lùnastal, VE 7,985 by sheep-keeping households of the north-east. Known for its wool market.

Baile gharbh is a large market town of the north-east and the seat of its province. It has been a wool market since the Holy Age, and the moor towns of Cnoc chaol and Àth fhada bring their flocks and cheese to it. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and has no walls, trusting to Baile Mòr dhìreach close by.

Ceann dhubh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,416

Founded 26 an Cèitean, LE 1,359 by Ròdaich fishers of the black headland. Known for its harbour under the black headland.

Ceann dhubh is a harbour under a dark headland, the port of Baile gharbh province, whose boats work the cold waters of the northern coast. Travellers on the coast road break their journey at An Leòmhann Buidhe a short way west, and the inn buys most of the harbour's catch. The harbour was deepened in the Age of Strangers to take the humans' ore ships, and has been too large for its trade ever since.

Cnoc chaol

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,754

Founded 16 an t-Ògmhios, LE 807 by goatherds of the northern hills. Known for its goat cheese for Baile gharbh.

Cnoc chaol, the narrow hill, is a small herding town of the north. It is not the southern Cnoc chaol that gave Tonn Mhòr its name. Its people keep the druid schools of the Old Faith and send their cheese and kids to the market at Baile gharbh.

Siorrachd Baile gheal

Àth fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,647

Founded 6 an Cèitean, LE 20 by ford-keepers of the road to Inis thais. Known for its ford on the pilgrims' road to Lia Fàil.

Àth fhiadhaich of the south-west is a ford on the pilgrimage road from Caol leathan to the temple of Lia Fàil at Inis thais. It grew from a single house of the long quiet centuries into a small town that lives on the pilgrims. It keeps the order of the Stone.

Baile gheal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 19,129

Founded 27 an Giblean, VE 9,670 by households round a white-limed house. Known for its white cloth of the western plain.

A large white town of the western plain and the seat of Siorrachd Baile gheal. It is a city of the order of the Stone in all but name, and it trades cloth with Baile Mòr fhionn and the harbour of Inis thais.

Siorrachd Baile ghlas

Baile dhubh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 680

Founded 1 an Giblean, AE 69 by human administrators near Seann Warr. Known for the old clerks' town by Seann Warr.

Baile dhubh was built in the Age of Strangers as a clerks' town for the human administration near Seann Warr, where the fifth regiment is now stationed. After the Severance its Ròdaich people took up the order of the Stone, the Old Faith of the country around it. It has fewer than seven hundred people and lives on the garrison.

Baile ghlas

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 35,358

Founded 7 an Cèitean, VE 9,370 by boat-households of the Red Hill. Known for its rope-walks and sail-lofts.

Baile ghlas is a great harbour town on the capital shore and the seat of its province. Its rope-walks and sail-lofts have fitted ships for the capital since the Holy Age, and it claims, with no record to prove it, to have rigged the Sundering fleet. It has never been walled; the capital's walls stand close by.

Doire fhada

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,892

Founded 3 an t-Sultain, LE 360 by woodsmen of the capital shore. Known for its walled long grove.

Doire fhada, the long grove, is a walled village on the shore of Loch chrom near the capital, founded in the long quiet centuries. It was walled in the Age of Strangers to protect its grain stores. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Siorrachd Baile ghorm

Achadh fhionn

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,804

Founded 23 an Lùnastal, FE 1,069 by farmers of the south-east. Known for its fair field under Làrach an Dùin.

Achadh fhionn is a village of the south-east, founded in the Holy Age in a fair field under Làrach an Dùin. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits and leaves the ruin alone. Its people say the ruin was old when the first Ròdaich came.

Baile dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 8,916

Founded 7 an t-Samhain, VE 7,711 by households of the panther country. Known for its rope-walks and the panthers' road.

The deep town a short walk inland of Baile ghorm, a settlement of the Ancient Age to which the harbour's rope-walks and timber-yards were later moved to be clear of storms. The panthers' migration road, Imrich nam Pantar, crosses its fields, and the townsfolk shut their stock in when the cats pass. It follows the order of the Stone and works almost entirely for the harbour and its fleet.

  • 15 am Faoilleach, VE 7,770 — The panther season kept at Baile dhomhain

Baile ghorm

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 23,309

Founded 22 an Gearran, FE 837 by farming kindreds of the south-eastern downs. Known for its south-eastern grain and wool market.

Baile ghorm is the market of its shire, a large open town without walls where the south-eastern farms bring their grain and wool. Its people keep the Old Spirits, the oldest folk rite of the island, and household shrines to the ancestors outnumber its spirit-houses. Achadh fhionn is its nearest field-village, and the ruin of Làrach an Dùin stands in its hinterland, left alone by custom.

  • 23 an t-Iuchar, FE 2,391 — Baile ghorm's penance
  • 16 an t-Samhain, LE 1,064 — The blue dyers of Baile ghorm
  • 13 am Màrt, LE 1,139 — The Baile ghorm blue fades
  • 18 an Giblean, AE 120 — Ore-lamps from Baile ghorm

Baile ghorm

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 27,580

Founded 7 an t-Ògmhios, VE 5,945 by salt-makers of the southern shore. Known for the third fleet's anchorage and wolf-post quays.

A landing of drying-racks and boat-sheds on the southern coast, Baile ghorm grew through the Holy Age into the largest harbour between the capital and the eastern capes. Its people keep the order of the Stone, whose stone is Clach, and its quays are lined with the wolf-head posts, for the wolf of the Fianna, that mark a harbour of that order. Since the Long War it has been the station of An treas cabhlach, the third fleet, and its yards now do more work on the crown's hulls than on the town's own boats. Its smaller twin, Baile dhomhain, lies a short walk inland and sends it timber and rope.

Cnoc bhàn

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 10,718

Founded 23 an Dùbhlachd, LE 250 by the hill-lords of Baile ghorm. Known for the market above the mill-race.

A walled pale hill in the south-east above the long mill-race of Muileann fhada, which grinds its grain. The walls were raised when the road from Làrach an Dùin became unsafe. It keeps the Old Spirits and is the market of the south-eastern farms. It sends the pearls of the south-eastern shallows and the clay of its fields to other markets.

  • 28 an Giblean, LE 1,051 — The market above the mill-race

Muileann fhada

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,280

Founded 16 an t-Samhain, LE 617 by millers of the house of Tormod mac Ruairidh. Known for the long mill-race and first-sack offering.

A long mill-race cut beside a south-eastern stream gave the town its name and its living, grinding the grain of the farms about the other Baile ghorm. Its walls were raised in the Age of Strangers, when the roads past Làrach an Dùin carried ore-wagons and the thieves who followed them. It keeps the Old Spirits, and the millers still leave the first sack of each season at the race-head for the ancestors. Cnoc bhàn on the hill above buys most of its flour.

Siorrachd Baile ìseal

Àth bheag

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 932

Founded 14 an Giblean, SE 9 by Tuathaich families sent north at the Severance. Known for a ford settled after the Severance.

A small ford settlement founded by Tuathaich families who came north at the Severance. It has fewer than a thousand people. It trades with Baile ìseal and Baile òg, the other Tuathaich towns of its province.

Baile ìseal

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 17,099

Founded 16 an t-Sultain, LE 1,567 by Ròdaich farmers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the low walled town of the north-west.

A low walled town in the north-west, the seat of Siorrachd Baile ìseal, resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It follows the faith of the Church and is one of the larger Tuathaich towns.

  • 2 an t-Ògmhios, AE 89 — Baile ìseal sends its people

Baile òg

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 2,885

Founded 5 an t-Samhain, SE 4 by Tuathaich families sent north at the Severance. Known for the first Tuathaich-built houses.

Baile òg, "the young town", was built by Tuathaich families who arrived after the Severance and found no empty village to take. It stands a short way from the larger Tuathaich town of Baile ìseal and has always leaned on it. Its houses are the first the Tuathaich built for themselves on the island rather than inherited.

Doire gheal

village · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 830

Founded 10 an Dàmhair, AE 65 by human settlers of the Age of Strangers. Known for its house of one of the oldest human families.

A small white oak grove settled by humans in the early years after the Crossing, one of the few human foundations of the north-west. Its people stayed through the Severance and are among the oldest human families on the island. It follows the faith of the Church.

Siorrachd Baile mhin

Baile mhin

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 20,963

Founded 17 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,685 by Ròdaich river-folk of the north-east. Known for its sheltered river quays of the north-east.

Baile mhin is a river town on the Abhainn bheag in the north-east and the seat of its province, founded in the Holy Age. Its quays are sheltered and its trade steady, and its barges go down to Caol chrom at the river mouth. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith, and the old landing of Seann Vell lies within its province.

  • 13 am Faoilleach, AE 54 — Baile mhin ships the eastern ore

Seann Vell

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,910

Founded 1 an Gearran, VE 1,201 by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for its old landing stones and seal-hunters.

Seann Vell of Baile mhin is a small river landing on a Seann-Dhaoine site on the Abhainn bheag in the north-east, a short way above the river mouth at Caol chrom, resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age. It lives on the seal-hunt at the river mouth and the fishing. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

  • 26 an t-Sultain, VE 2,285 — The north-eastern Seann Vell

Siorrachd Baile Mòr dhomhain

Achadh dhìreach

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 776

Founded 16 an Cèitean, VE 303 by hill-folk of the high valleys. Known for its straight fields of the restored kingdom.

Achadh dhìreach holds the oldest hearths of the high valleys, and it was laid out anew in straight fields by the restored kingdom, when the diggings were worked to the full again and the towns of the plain needed feeding. It is small, fewer than eight hundred people. It feeds Baile Mòr àrsaidh.

  • 16 an Cèitean, VE 303 — The first hearths of the high valleys
  • 13 an t-Sultain, VE 4,540 — The stained cloth of Achadh dhìreach
  • 7 an t-Iuchar, VE 6,389 — The basket burning at Achadh dhìreach

Àth chaol

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,924

Founded 5 an t-Sultain, LE 519 by the ford-wardens of Baile Mòr dhomhain. Known for its walled ford on the city's north road.

One of the island's many narrow fords, this one a walled post on the north road into Baile Mòr dhomhain. The city built its walls to hold the crossing in the troubles before the Severance, and it is still garrisoned in name. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Àth chiar

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 5,863

Founded 30 an Lùnastal, LE 1,347 by the ford-guards of Baile Mòr dhomhain. Known for its carriers of the west road.

A dusky ford on the west road out of Baile Mòr dhomhain, walled against the roads' thieves in the Age of Strangers. It is a carriers' town, and the road-house An Taigh-seinnse Reòta at Muileann fhada lies a short way down the road. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Àth ghlas

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,648

Founded 16 an Giblean, LE 149 by the grey-stone quarrymen. Known for the worked-out grey quarry.

A ford over grey water on the road between Baile Mòr dhomhain and the south, it grew up around a quarry whose pale-grey stone faces half the city's houses. The quarry is now worked out, and the town has shrunk to a waystation for carriers. Its people keep to the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Àth mhòr

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,601

Founded 26 an Cèitean, FE 1,598 by Ròdaich ford-keepers of the northern plain. Known for its ford on the northern tavern road.

One of several towns of this name, this Àth mhòr carries the tavern road across the river near An Taigh-seinnse Reòta. It was a waypoint on the mining roads in the Holy Age and a militia halt in the years before the war. It trades oak from Doire dhìreach down the road to the towns of the plain.

Àth shean

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,324

Founded 8 an t-Ògmhios, FE 2,486 by boatmen of the Baile Mòr dhomhain river. Known for the river landing of Baile Mòr dhomhain.

The old ford and landing that served Baile Mòr dhomhain before the city had quays of its own. Barges from the landing carry the city's goods to the coast, and the boatmen's guild here is older than the city's walls. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith like its great neighbour and is counted, for most purposes, as the city's river-port.

Baile Mòr àrsaidh

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 5,986

Founded 16 an t-Samhain, FE 1,337 by Ròdaich traders of the northern plain. Known for its ancient market of the northern plain.

Baile Mòr àrsaidh is an ancient market city of the northern plain, ranked a city for its age rather than its size. Its market was old in the Holy Age. It takes oak from Doire dhìreach and grain from Achadh dhìreach.

Baile Mòr dhomhain

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 17,651

Founded 24 an t-Samhain, FE 101 by the lords of the deep river. Known for the deep-river city and its fords.

A walled city with a citadel on a deep river in the north, the seat of Siorrachd Baile Mòr dhomhain. It was one of the great market cities of the north through the Holy Age and the Sundering and a centre of the human administration in the Age of Strangers. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and holds its four fords and its river landing at Àth shean. It is the market town of the northern hills and the second cattle-market of the island. The white marble of its hills is quarried nearby, and the town is known for its books.

  • 22 an t-Samhain, FE 1,122 — The market at the fords of Baile Mòr dhomhain

Baile òg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,790

Founded 25 am Màrt, LE 110 by carters of Baile Mòr dhomhain. Known for a carters' stop between two cities.

A small young town on the road between Baile Mòr dhomhain and Baile Mòr àrsaidh, grown from a carters' stable. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and lives by changing horses.

Cuan bheag

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 18,125

Founded 1 an Dùbhlachd, LE 1,554 by river traders of the northern country. Known for its sheltered river mooring and the northern watch.

Cuan bheag, the small harbour, is a river port on the upper Abhainn ìseal. It was a fishing water until the Age of Strangers, when human traders wanted a sheltered mooring on this side of the island, with the river open to the sea at Ros gheal, and it grew busy. The restored kingdom built its citadel to watch the northern approaches, and the town has since become one of the larger river ports of the province. Its people keep the Old Faith in the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Doire dhìreach

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 8,421

Founded 1 an Dàmhair, FE 647 by Ròdaich woodwards of the Baile Mòr dhomhain plain. Known for its straight-grown oak for keels.

An oak grove kept by woodward families, whose trees grow tall and true beyond the common run. It is told of the Sundering that the shipwrights sent to Doire dhìreach for keels when the ocean ships were built, and the village has told that tale of itself ever since. It has grown into a large village of timber-yards and cooperages, serving Àth mhòr and Baile Mòr àrsaidh.

Inis leathan

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,410

Founded 29 an Giblean, LE 1,298 by ferrymen of the broad isle. Known for its ferrymen of the broad isle.

Inis leathan is a village on a broad island in the lower Abhainn fhionn near the north coast, founded in the long quiet centuries by ferrymen who ran boats to either bank. In the Age of Strangers its ferry carried supplies to the tavern and mill at Muileann fhada. It still keeps the ferry, and little else.

Muileann fhada

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,702

Founded 8 an Dàmhair, FE 550 by millers of the northern mining road. Known for An Taigh-seinnse Reòta on the mining road.

Muileann fhada, the long mill, is a small walled town on the old mining road of the north. An Taigh-seinnse Reòta stands at its edge, one of the great taverns of the old circuit. Colbh Cnoc chiar stands to the west, and the town's people say the stone's two words are older than any mill.

Siorrachd Baile Mòr mhòr

Baile Mòr mhòr

city · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 35,852

Founded 13 an t-Sultain, VE 7,939 by households of the northern plain. Known for the great walled city of the north.

Baile Mòr mhòr is the great city of the north, walled and crowned by a citadel, and the seat of its province. It held one of the royal granaries in the Holy Age and was a centre of the human administration in the Age of Strangers. Since the Severance it has stood close to the Tuathaich country to the west, the largest Ròdaich city on that frontier.

Caol ìseal

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,953

Founded 25 am Faoilleach, FE 1,428 by the strait-watchers of the north coast. Known for the strait watch-fire.

A small harbour-village on the northern strait, with a citadel built to watch the channel. It served Baile Mòr mhòr as a signal-station and watch-post, and it has never been more. It keeps the Old Spirits of the Ròdaich, and the watch-fire on its citadel is still lit on the old feast nights.

Dùn thais

city · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 3,755

Founded 10 an Dàmhair, FE 1,454 by custodians of the northern coast. Known for the northernmost Ròdaich citadel.

Dùn thais of the north is the northernmost Ròdaich citadel, raised by the Holy Age custodians on the northern coast. Since the Severance it has watched the Tuathaich country. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits.

Siorrachd Baile ruadh

Baile ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 19,896

Founded 3 an Dàmhair, FE 971 by red-earth farmers of the east. Known for its red-earth fields of the east.

A red town of the east and the seat of Siorrachd Baile ruadh. It keeps the Old Spirits and trades grain with Achadh naomh.

  • 13 an Lùnastal, FE 2,909 — The watch-tower at Baile ruadh

Cnoc fhionn

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 11,165

Founded 25 an t-Samhain, VE 3,715 by hill households of the east. Known for its fair-hill barley and ale.

Cnoc fhionn, the fair hill, is a large town of sheltered farms in the north-east. It has been settled since the Ancient Age and keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits. Its barley and ale go down to the harbour at Seann Tarr.

  • 5 an t-Iuchar, VE 3,751 — The first dog graves

Siorrachd Caol bheag

Baile bhàn

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 6,025

Founded 21 an Giblean, LE 1,634 by fullers of the northern coast. Known for its bleached cloth from the fulling-mills.

A town of fulling-mills and white cloth between the port-city of Ros chiar and the city of Baile Mòr dhìreach. Its fullers bleached wool for the harbours of the north coast and still do, though in smaller measure since the trade moved to Inis mhòr. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Baile Mòr dhìreach

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,107

Founded 8 an Gearran, FE 1,732 by custodians of the north-eastern road. Known for its walls on the straight road.

Baile Mòr dhìreach of Caol bheag is a walled town with a citadel, built by Holy Age custodians where the north-eastern road runs straight. It is small for a city, but it holds the road and the market between Inis mhòr and Baile gharbh. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Caol bheag

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,189

Founded 15 am Màrt, FE 477 by fishers of the north coast. Known for the elder Caol bheag on the strait.

A small harbour on the northern strait, older than its far larger namesake inland and the one that gave that town its name. It keeps the Old Spirits and is a quiet fishing town, though An ceathramh rèisimeid, stationed at the larger Caol bheag, sends its patrols here. It stands on Eilean fhada, the long island off the north coast, and the strait it is named for is the sound between that island and Rodos.

  • 13 an t-Sultain, AE 55 — A brig lost in the mist
  • 9 an Dàmhair, AE 145 — Caol bheag's empty quay

Caol bheag

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 42,649

Founded 14 an Lùnastal, VE 7,737 by fishing households of the north coast. Known for its river port, where the fourth regiment lies.

Caol bheag is a river port of more than forty thousand on the narrows of the Abhainn ghorm, crowned by a citadel and the seat of its province; its barges run down to Ros chiar at the river mouth. The fourth regiment, raised in the Long War, is stationed here. The mills of Muileann bheag and the wool of Cnoc chiar pass through its quays.

Siorrachd Caol fhiadhaich

Caol fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 19,115

Founded 12 an t-Iuchar, VE 6,870 by salmon-trappers of the south-west. Known for its strait-pilots and the harbour wolf-stone.

A harbour on a wild strait whose pilots earned their living guiding ships through the rocks. It is the seat of Siorrachd Caol fhiadhaich and a large town of the order of the Stone, trading with the great tavern-village of Doire shean on its road. The strait pilots still take no ship through without an offering to Clach, the Stone, at the harbour wolf-stone.

Cnoc dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,587

Founded 4 am Màrt, LE 1,118 by carters of Caol fhiadhaich. Known for its carters' stop on the south-west road.

A small town on a straight hill road between Caol fhiadhaich and the great mill-town of Muileann bheag. It follows the order of the Stone and is a stop for carters.

Muileann bheag

fort · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 13,749

Founded 31 an Cèitean, LE 1,295 by wardens of the panther roads. Known for its citadel north of the panther roads.

Muileann bheag is a fort with a citadel north of Baile dhomhain, whose fields the panthers of Imrich nam Pantar cross. It is not the Muileann bheag of the northern lighthouse. Travellers stop at Am Buabhall Fortanach nearby, and the first fleet lies at Àth gharbh a short way west.

Siorrachd Caol gharbh

Caol chrom

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,192

Founded 13 an Dùbhlachd, LE 1,275 by the garrison of the bent strait. Known for its fortified bent strait.

Caol chrom is a fortified harbour on a bent strait of the north-east, walled and given a citadel in the long quiet centuries. It is a city by rank but small in people, and its garrison has always outnumbered its fishermen. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith. Its few townsmen boil soap and blow glass for the hill towns. Its headmen and Caol gharbh's meet at Coinneachadh na h-Amhaich, the stone on the neck of land between the two harbours, to settle the dues of the strait.

  • 7 an Gearran, SE 48 — The north-eastern harbours

Caol gharbh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 26,717

Founded 10 am Màrt, VE 9,451 by Ròdaich seafarers of the rough strait. Known for its boatyards on the rough strait.

Caol gharbh is a walled harbour on the rough strait and the seat of its province, a village in name but a town of twenty-seven thousand in fact. Its boatyards take oak from Doire chaol and build the heavy boats the strait demands. Its quarrel with Seann Bhrenn next door is as old as the rolls. Its headmen and Caol chrom's meet at Coinneachadh na h-Amhaich, the stone on the neck of land between the two harbours, to settle the dues of the strait.

Doire chaol

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,925

Founded 22 an Lùnastal, LE 762 by woodwards for Caol gharbh's yards. Known for its oak for Caol gharbh's boatyards.

A village in a narrow oakwood that has sent timber to the boatyards of Caol gharbh since the yards were opened. It has always been small and has always been owed money by the yards. Its families also hunt the oakwood, and their venison goes down to Caol gharbh with the timber. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Siorrachd Caol ìseal

Baile shean

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,859

Founded 13 an Dùbhlachd, FE 727 by Ròdaich fishers of the northern shore. Known for its old quay of the northern shore.

Baile shean is an old quay on the northern shore and the port of its province. The inn An Taigh-seinnse Reòta lies inland on the road south, and its pickled spinach goes out through the quay. It is one of several places named Baile shean.

Caol ìseal

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 16,600

Founded 21 am Màrt, FE 1,450 by salt-makers of the northern coast. Known for its salt pans of the low strait.

Caol ìseal is a harbour town on a low strait of the north coast and the seat of its province. Its salt pans have supplied the northern fisheries since the Holy Age. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits. Bog-iron dug behind the pans feeds its forges, which cast field-guns for the regiments.

  • 31 an Cèitean, LE 1,369 — The Caol ìseal fishers go east

Cnoc bhàn

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 3,395

Founded 21 am Màrt, LE 35 by fishers of Caol ìseal. Known for its white-hill kelp and herring.

Cnoc bhàn grew as an overflow of the harbour at Caol ìseal, a white hill with a landing at its foot. Its boats work the kelp beds and the herring of the northern shore. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits and has never needed walls.

Cnoc uaine

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,458

Founded 17 an t-Ògmhios, LE 1,305 by the garrison of the north-coast road. Known for its hill fort over the north-coast road.

Cnoc uaine of Caol ìseal is a hill fort over the north-coast road, raised in the long quiet centuries and walled since. Its garrison watched the road through the Age of Strangers. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits.

Siorrachd Caol leathan

Baile Mòr fhionn

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 18,849

Founded 6 an t-Samhain, FE 584 by the lords of the western plain. Known for the fair citadel of the western plain.

A great fair walled city of the west, seat of lords before the kingdom and a fortress since. Its citadel was held by Ròdaich forces through the war that ended in the Severance, and it is a city of the order of the Stone. It is the chief market of the plain between the capital and the western harbours. Its own vineyards give the plain's wine, and the town salts meat, makes boots and dips candles.

Caol leathan

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 8,622

Founded 12 am Faoilleach, VE 6,883 by seal-hunting households of the western shore. Known for its strait tolls and the western pilots' guild.

Caol leathan grew on the wide strait that gives it its name, where the western pilots of the Holy Age took a toll from every boat bound for the capital's waters. Its walls and citadel were raised in the Age of Sundering to hold the strait, and were manned again when the strangers' ships began to use it after the Crossing. It is the northern anchor of the country of the Stone, and its druids look south to the temple of Lia Fàil at Inis thais for their rite.

Siorrachd Caol mhin

Caol mhin

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 6,648

Founded 17 am Màrt, FE 1,345 by Ròdaich seafarers of Baile Mòr mhòr. Known for its calm-strait harbour of Baile Mòr mhòr.

Caol mhin is the harbour of Baile Mòr mhòr on the calm strait, and its fortunes have always followed the city's. It is walled against raiders from the sea. Its quays, which stand on Eilean chrom across the calm strait from the city, load wool and hides from the northern uplands.

  • 11 an Giblean, AE 76 — Quarantine at Caol mhin

Siorrachd Caol mhòr

Àth fhionn

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 844

Founded 25 an Cèitean, AE 14 by human traders, as a waystation. Known for a human waystation at the fair ford.

Àth fhionn was a waystation of human traders on the road north, built in the Age of Strangers at a fair ford. The Tuathaich kept it after the Severance. It is small, fewer than a thousand people, and its inn is still built in the humans' manner.

Àth leathan

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 2,686

Founded 24 am Faoilleach, LE 925 by Ròdaich drovers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for a drovers' ford in the north.

The northern Àth leathan is a drovers' ford resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It is not the battlefield of the Long War, which lies far to the south-west, and its people have spent a generation correcting travellers. It follows the faith of the Church.

  • 11 am Faoilleach, VE 7,140 — The flint road

Baile àrsaidh

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 2,857

Founded 15 am Màrt, FE 1,651 by Ròdaich shore-lords, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for its old walls in the Tuathaich north.

An ancient walled town near the harbour of Caol mhòr, one of the Ròdaich towns resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. The walls are older than any Ròdaich memory of them, and the Tuathaich have kept them. It follows the faith of the Church.

Baile dhubh

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 1,709

Founded 4 an t-Samhain, AE 86 by human colliers of the northern seams. Known for its coal pits of the northern holdouts.

Baile dhubh, "the black town", was built by human colliers in the Age of Strangers on one of the northern coal seams, which the humans worked alongside the vein in the south. After the Severance it passed to the Tuathaich with the rest of the north. Before the Long War it was one of the towns that refused the new fuel and kept working the last seams that would still yield.

Caol mhòr

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 42,002

Founded 31 an Dùbhlachd, VE 7,785 by Ròdaich harbour-folk; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for its place as the chief harbour of the Tuathaich.

Caol mhòr, the great strait, was a Ròdaich harbour from the Ancient Age. After the Severance it became the chief port of the Tuathaich, and it is now their largest town. Its yards take timber from Doire mhin, and its people keep the faith of the Church.
