Doire gharbh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 12,372

Founded 2 an Dàmhair, FE 1,695 by Ròdaich shipwrights' woodwards. Known for its rough oak for the western fleet.

A large walled village in rough oakwood that has supplied timber to the yards at Cuan shean since the Holy Age. When the fleet of Cuan shean was raised in the Long War its hulls were cut here. It follows the order of Manannan, as does most of the west.

Siorrachd Doire chaol

Àth fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,445

Founded 14 an t-Sultain, FE 995 by Ròdaich ford-keepers of the capital. Known for its wild ford on the capital's south road.

Àth fhiadhaich is the wild ford on the south road out of Cathair dhearg, a town of ten thousand that grew as the capital grew. Its crossing was paved in the Holy Age, and the road over it carries the capital's trade toward the southern coast. It follows the capital's order, the order of Macha, and its shrine keepers take part in the rites at Cathair dhearg.

  • 21 an Dàmhair, FE 1,001 — The fight at Àth fhiadhaich

Doire chaol

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 24,225

Founded 3 an Giblean, AE 17 by carters of the capital's road. Known for the capital's household village.

Doire chaol was a carters' village outside the capital in the Age of Strangers, and after the Severance it was laid out anew on a narrow oak strip by the Abhainn dhomhain south of the capital, to house the families of the royal household. It grew into a large village, and in the kingdom's fourth decade it was cut out of the shire of Baile chiar as a shire of its own, the only shire made since the shires were first drawn. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha.

  • 20 an Giblean, AE 35 — The carters of Doire chaol

Siorrachd Doire chiar

Cill dhearg

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,761

Founded 7 an t-Samhain, FE 549 by druids of the schools. Known for its red temple-house by the old bridge.

A temple village of red stone near Drochaid Ros fhionn, whose house of the druid schools gave shelter to travellers crossing the old bridge when the river trade was busy. As the trade failed and the bridge fell out of use, the village shrank to its temple-house and a few farms. Its druids still keep a lamp at the bridge-end.

Cnoc ìseal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,684

Founded 7 an t-Samhain, LE 1,261 by flax-growers of the north. Known for its flax fields and linen.

Cnoc ìseal, the low hill, is a small town of the north-east given to flax and linen. It was founded in the long quiet centuries and has changed little since. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Doire chiar

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 23,587

Founded 8 an Giblean, VE 9,506 by oak-keepers of the north-east. Known for its disputations under the oaks.

A dusky oak grove grown into a large village, the seat of Siorrachd Doire chiar. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith, and its druids are said to hold their disputations under the oldest trees.

  • 8 an Giblean, VE 9,506 — Doire chiar
  • 23 an t-Ògmhios, LE 484 — Eilidh Dhubh's tracts
  • 30 an Giblean, AE 90 — The last disputation at Doire chiar

Muileann fhada

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,677

Founded 10 am Màrt, LE 785 by millers of Doire chiar. Known for its flour for Doire chiar.

A long mill in the north-east beside Muileann dhearg, grinding for the large village of Doire chiar. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Siorrachd Doire fhada

Cuan uaine

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 6,529

Founded 23 an Dùbhlachd, FE 2,534 by Ròdaich custodians of the capital's east. Known for the temple of Macha on the Abhainn fhionn.

Cuan uaine, whose name means the green harbour, is a walled temple city on the Abhainn fhionn east of the capital, fortified in the Holy Age to guard the river road to the eastern shore. Its temple of Macha is much visited by those who cannot reach the capital's. The barracks town of Inis mhòr lies just upriver to the north. Its copyists and tailors work for the capital.

  • 5 an t-Sultain, AE 150 — Cuan uaine opens its quays

Doire fhada

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 21,905

Founded 27 am Faoilleach, FE 2,013 by oak-cutters of the capital's forests. Known for its ship-timber and the fenced oak.

A long oak grove east of the capital cut for ship-timber since the Holy Age, and the shipwrights who built the Sundering fleet are said to have taken their keels here. The village grew enormous without changing its name, and it is now the seat of Siorrachd Doire fhada and a river port of the capital's order, Macha's, on the Abhainn fhionn. The grove itself is mostly gone, and the village keeps one old oak fenced by the river quay.

Siorrachd Doire fhiadhaich

Cnoc shean

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,179

Founded 6 an t-Sultain, FE 1,217 by Ròdaich herders of the south. Known for its market common on the old hill.

Cnoc shean, the old hill, is a small town of the south, settled since the Holy Age. Its common holds the market of the farms around it. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Doire fhiadhaich

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 27,501

Founded 19 an Lùnastal, FE 1,981 by the oak-keepers of the south. Known for its timber for Cathair fhada.

A wild oak grove in the south, grown into a very large village and the seat of Siorrachd Doire fhiadhaich. It follows the order of Macha and supplies timber to the city of Cathair fhada close by.

  • 15 an Dàmhair, AE 31 — Meal-carts at Doire fhiadhaich

Siorrachd Doire fhionn

Achadh àrsaidh

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,452

Founded 12 an t-Ògmhios, FE 821 by Ròdaich herders on an older field. Known for its field-walls older than any memory.

Achadh àrsaidh, the ancient field, was named by Ròdaich herders who found its field-walls already standing and old when they came. Who laid them is not known. Tiormachd Achadh shean, the Long Drought, struck it in the Age of Strangers and parched its hay-meadows for three dry seasons running. It has stayed a small village of cattle and hay on the eastern uplands, keeping the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits and its walls in repair.

Àth ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,509

Founded 25 an t-Sultain, FE 2,335 by cattle-drovers of the eastern hills. Known for the drovers' ford and cattle fair.

A red-banked ford where the drovers' road crosses a stream in the east, it has been a cattle-market since the Holy Age. It keeps the Old Spirits of the Ròdaich, and the drovers still pour a cup into the ford before driving a herd across. The town trades beasts to Seann Dunn on the coast and hides to Baile shean. Furs and hides from the eastern hills are sold at its fair.

Àth uaine

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,572

Founded 25 an Giblean, LE 1,715 by the wardens of the Achadh shean road. Known for its garrisoned green ford.

A small garrison town at the green ford on the road between Doire fhionn and Achadh shean. Its citadel is larger than the town needs, for the ford was once fought over, though by whom is not remembered. Tiormachd Achadh shean, the Long Drought, struck it in the Age of Strangers, and it lives now on toll and on the soldiers who still keep the tower.

Baile dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 9,699

Founded 1 an t-Samhain, LE 251 by carters of the Seann Dunn road. Known for its straight road to Seann Dunn.

A town of one straight road running down to Seann Dunn, whose carters take the dyed cloth of Baile ghorm to the harbour. It is a town of nearly ten thousand. It keeps the Old Spirits.

Baile ghorm

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 4,277

Founded 22 an Lùnastal, LE 309 by Ròdaich dyers from Achadh shean. Known for its woad dyers and blue-washed houses.

Baile ghorm grew up around woad pits and dye-houses, and its houses were long washed blue from the vats. It sent cloth to Seann Dunn for shipping and yarn to Achadh shean for weaving. The Old Spirits, the old rite of the ancestors, are strong here, and the dyers still leave a first skein at the hearth-stone each season.

Baile shean

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,687

Founded 5 an Dàmhair, FE 1,655 by keepers of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar. Known for the keepers of the sacred forest's edge.

An old town beside Coille Naomh Muileann chiar, the forest marked sacred before any faith claimed it. Its people have kept the forest's edge since the Holy Age and keep the Old Spirits, though the forest is now held by the druid schools.

Cill àrsaidh

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,982

Founded 19 an Giblean, FE 2,448 by keepers of the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits. Known for its ancient cell of the ancestor rite.

Cill àrsaidh of the north is an old cell of the ancestor rite, founded in the Holy Age and never much more than a village around its shrine. It lies inland of the Hawk bay and has kept to the Old Spirits while its neighbours took up the Hawk order and the rite of Mòd. The shrine keepers are hereditary. Its people gather amber on the strands of the Hawk bay.

Cnoc ghorm

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 8,412

Founded 22 an Dàmhair, FE 734 by bee-keepers of the north. Known for its blue hill and bee-keeping.

Cnoc ghorm of Doire fhionn is a town of the north-central country, founded in the Holy Age. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits and its bees, whose wax lit the shrines at Cill àrsaidh before dubhan lamps came.

Doire fhionn

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 21,604

Founded 20 am Màrt, FE 397 by Ròdaich woodsmen of the east. Known for its great oak grove of the east.

Doire fhionn of the east is the seat of its province, a great village of the Holy Age in an oak grove; for all its size it has never been raised to the rank of a town. Its oaks are felled and planted under rules older than the kingdom. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits, and the old field-village of Achadh àrsaidh lies to its north.

  • 10 an Gearran, VE 3,700 — The deer-drives of the eastern forest
  • 5 an Dàmhair, AE 107 — Doire fhionn walks for water

Doire fhionn

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 13,873

Founded 4 an t-Samhain, FE 1,149 by the oak-keepers of the Old Spirits. Known for an uncut grove of the ancestors.

A fair oak grove in the north, the seat of Siorrachd Doire fhionn and a large village of the Old Spirits. The grove has never been cut for ship-timber, its keepers holding it for the ancestors, and it lies on the road between Cathair naomh and the Tuathaich line.

  • 26 an Lùnastal, LE 5 — The oaks of Doire fhionn

Muileann ruadh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,120

Founded 29 an Giblean, FE 1,583 by Ròdaich millers of the north. Known for its red mill and border citadel.

Muileann ruadh of Doire fhionn is a mill town of the north-central country, founded in the Holy Age. Its citadel was raised after the Severance to watch the Tuathaich border. It keeps the Hawk order of the Old Faith.

Tobar ghorm

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 6,465

Founded 27 am Faoilleach, FE 2,921 by Ròdaich well-keepers of the northern road. Known for its blue spring on the northern road.

A village around a blue spring on the road running north toward the Tuathaich country, and the last Ròdaich water on that road. Since the Severance it has traded with both sides of the line and has been trusted by neither. It is not the larger Tobar ghorm of the wool fairs, and it resents the confusion.

Siorrachd Doire ghlas

Cnoc mhòr

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 5,564

Founded 5 an t-Sultain, LE 1,233 by Ròdaich herders; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for its keepers of the Muileann bheag light.

Cnoc mhòr of Doire ghlas is a Tuathaich town of the north coast, founded by Ròdaich herders in the long quiet centuries and resettled after the Severance. Its people supply the keepers of Taigh-solais Muileann bheag. It keeps the faith of the Church.

  • 17 an Lùnastal, AE 97 — Cnoc mhòr walks south

Doire fhionn

village · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 5,264

Founded 5 an Dàmhair, LE 482 by Ròdaich woodwards; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for its pale oaks and Tuathaich hearth-tellings.

A Ròdaich village in a grove of pale oaks, left empty at the Severance and resettled by Tuathaich families sent north. Its people keep the Tuathaich Church, and it is one of the northern households where the voyage of Naomh Breandan is still told at the hearth, a telling the Ròdaich druids call superstition. It lives on timber and on the fort at Cnoc leathan nearby.

Doire ghlas

village · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 40,740

Founded 26 an Giblean, VE 7,793 by Ròdaich oak-cutters, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the great Tuathaich gathering-village.

A small Ròdaich village in a grey oak grove until the Severance, when the families shepherded north were gathered here before being sent on, and so many stayed that it became the largest settlement in the Tuathaich homeland almost at once. It never took a town's name, and the Tuathaich keep it a village in speech on purpose. It is the seat of Siorrachd Doire ghlas and the heart of the Tuathaich Church, whose priests are said to hold the oldest copy of the voyage of Naomh Breandan here; the library has asked to copy it and been refused. Its wool mills, built with the Moot's money, make the grey twill of the north.

Siorrachd Doire mhin

Baile bhàn

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 9,453

Founded 19 an Dùbhlachd, LE 1,238 by Ròdaich traders of Doire mhin. Known for its white walls on the Muileann ghlas road.

Baile bhàn is a white town of nine thousand near Cathair mhòr, on the road toward Muileann ghlas. Before the last battle of the Long War the kingdom's columns marched through it. It follows the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Baile chrom

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,296

Founded 24 am Faoilleach, LE 270 by the tithe-reeves of Cathair mhòr. Known for the walled tithe-granaries.

A walled town on a bend of the road below Cathair mhòr, raised to store and guard the tithe-grain of the Doire mhin country. Its walls were strengthened when the human administration raised the tithe, and it is remembered that the grain was guarded but not shared. It keeps the order of Macha and serves Cill fhada and Muileann ruadh as their market. The dubhan works under its walls supply the forges of the gulf, and the town boils soap.

  • 11 an Gearran, AE 74 — The Green Death at Baile chrom

Cathair mhòr

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 6,637

Founded 28 an Cèitean, FE 2,147 by the lords of Doire mhin. Known for the citadel on the capital's north road.

A hill-city with a citadel close to the capital, raised by lords of the Doire mhin country who held the roads north of Cathair dhearg. It has always been a garrison town and was one of the strongholds from which the war before the Severance was fought. It follows the order of Macha and draws on the tithe-granaries of Baile chrom and the great village of Doire mhin. It is not the Cathair mhòr of the third regiment, which lies further east. Its glass-house is the largest on the island.

Cnoc chiar

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,716

Founded 10 an t-Samhain, LE 1,603 by herders of Doire mhin. Known for its hill pastures of Doire mhin.

A small dusky hill between Doire mhin and Muileann ruadh, pastured by herders of the great village. It follows the order of Macha.

Cnoc ìseal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,411

Founded 31 an Cèitean, LE 43 by farmers of Doire mhin. Known for its hill farms by Muileann ghlas field.

Cnoc ìseal of Doire mhin is a small town of hill farms east of the capital, founded in the long quiet centuries. The field of Muileann ghlas, where An Cogadh Fada ended, lies just to the west, and the town's barns sheltered the wounded after the battle. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Doire mhin

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 33,558

Founded 10 an t-Ògmhios, FE 2,260 by the oak-keepers of the capital's north. Known for the great grove-village of the north road.

A smooth-barked oak grove north of the capital, grown into one of the largest settlements on the island while keeping its village name and customs. It is the seat of Siorrachd Doire mhin and follows the order of Macha. Its people farm for Cathair mhòr and send much of their grain to the tithe-granaries at Baile chrom.

  • 24 an t-Sultain, LE 555 — The burning of Doire mhin
  • 31 an Dùbhlachd, AE 21 — The last count at Doire mhin

Siorrachd Doire shean

Àth gharbh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,556

Founded 28 an t-Sultain, FE 1,855 by drovers of the western road. Known for the first fleet's walled ford town.

Àth gharbh, the rough ford, is a walled town of the south-west, a short walk from Doire shean and its great roadside tavern, Am Buabhall Fortanach. That tavern fortified with the others of the old mining circuit before the war of the Severance. Since An Cogadh Fada, A' chiad chabhlach has been stationed here and carries the town's name; its hulls lie in the harbour of Doire shean below.

  • 13 an Cèitean, DE 21 — A' chiad chabhlach raised

Doire shean

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 35,064

Founded 14 an Lùnastal, VE 6,018 by potters of the south-west coast. Known for Am Buabhall Fortanach and jugged buffalo.

An old oak grove in the south-west, grown into one of the largest villages on the island and the seat of Siorrachd Doire shean. At its heart is Am Buabhall Fortanach, the most famous tavern on the old roads, which serves jugged buffalo and has stood since the Holy Age. It is a harbour as well, where the hulls of the first fleet of Àth gharbh lie, and follows the order of the Stone. Rathad na Banrighinn, Queen Catrìona's stone road from the capital to Inis thais, runs through the village past the tavern.

Siorrachd Dùn chrom

Àth dhubh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 5,063

Founded 1 an t-Sultain, LE 777 by Ròdaich ferrymen of Dùn chrom. Known for the black ford and its walls.

The black ford takes its name from the dark water over the crossing. Walls were raised in the Age of Strangers, when the crossing carried much of the capital's traffic eastward. The Battle of Muileann ghlas, the last of An Cogadh Fada, was fought within sight of its walls.

Àth mhin

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,630

Founded 7 an t-Ògmhios, LE 1,064 by wardens of the Dùn chrom crossings. Known for the smooth ford and its citadel.

A walled town with a citadel at the smooth ford, one of a chain of crossings east of the capital. It was a quartering place for soldiers in the Age of Strangers and again in the Long War, when it held the kingdom's stores for the campaign that ended at Muileann ghlas. Its people are mostly carters and stable-keepers.

Baile chrom

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,068

Founded 5 am Màrt, LE 682 by herders from Dùn chrom. Known for Dùn chrom's stockyards.

The lesser of the two Baile chroms in the central midlands, this one lies under the citadel of Dùn chrom and grew as its stockyard. The fighting at Muileann ghlas in the last year of the Long War passed close enough that the town housed wounded for a season. It keeps the order of Macha.

Cnoc leathan

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,626

Founded 12 an Dàmhair, LE 1,189 by Ròdaich herders of Dùn chrom. Known for its lodgings and horse-lines for Fèill Muileann òg.

A modest town on the broad hill beside Muileann òg, whose people live for most of the year on herding and for one season on the fair. Since Fèill Muileann òg became the island's greatest gathering, Cnoc leathan has lodged the traders the fair town cannot hold and stabled their animals. It stood near the lines at Muileann ghlas and was emptied for the battle.

Dùn chrom

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 21,065

Founded 7 am Faoilleach, VE 8,124 by the lords of the bent hill. Known for the citadel above Muileann ghlas.

A fortified city on a crooked hill in the midlands, seat of Siorrachd Dùn chrom, with a citadel that commands the roads south of the capital. The last battle of the Long War, at Muileann ghlas, was fought within sight of its citadel, and the crown's commanders used its citadel as their headquarters. It follows the order of Macha and is served by the stockyard town of Baile chrom and the ford at Àth mhin.

Muileann ghlas

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,877

Founded 16 an t-Samhain, FE 748 by Ròdaich millers of Dùn chrom. Known for the last battle of the Long War.

The grey mill is an old grain town near the fair at Muileann òg and within a day of the capital. It is remembered above all for the Battle of Muileann ghlas, the second and last great battle of An Cogadh Fada, fought on its fields, in which the Tuathaich holdouts were broken. The battlefield, Àraich Muileann ghlas, lies just north-west of the town.

  • 19 an t-Iuchar, LE 1,274 — The battle of Muileann ghlas
  • 6 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22 — The camp by Muileann ghlas

Muileann òg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,667

Founded 10 am Faoilleach, FE 905 by carriers of the western road. Known for Fèill Muileann òg, the great fair.

Muileann òg, the young mill, stood beside the old ford-ground of the gathering in the Holy Age; it was burned in the War of the Roads and rebuilt as a market town. Its annual fair, Fèill Muileann òg, became the island's largest gathering. The field of Muileann ghlas, where An Cogadh Fada ended, lies close by. Rathad na Fèille, the fair road, was metalled from Cathair dhearg in the fair's first years.

  • 13 an Giblean, FE 999 — The War of the Roads begins at Muileann òg
  • 20 an Giblean, AE 131 — The old market at Muileann òg

Siorrachd Dùn dhearg

Àth àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,029

Founded 19 am Màrt, FE 1,894 by the ford-keepers of Dùn dhearg. Known for the pebble-cairn at the ford-stone.

An ancient ford in the east, between the mill town of Muileann leathan and Seann Mhorn on the coast. It keeps the Old Spirits and a ford-stone where travellers leave a pebble, and it has been a small crossing town since the Holy Age.

Cill bhàn

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,569

Founded 20 am Màrt, FE 276 by keepers of the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits. Known for its white cell of the ancestor rite.

Cill bhàn, the white cell, is a village of the Old Spirits' ancestor rite in the east, founded in the Holy Age. It lies near the hot springs and the silver workings of the vein country. It has kept its spirit-house through every age and every change of master.

Cnoc ghlas

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 3,914

Founded 21 an Dùbhlachd, FE 8 by quarriers for Dùn dhearg. Known for its grey stone for Dùn dhearg.

Cnoc ghlas is the grey hill whose stone built much of Dùn dhearg. It is a quarry town and lives by the city. Its quarrymen keep the Old Spirits' rites of the ancestors and will not open a new face without them.

  • 22 an Dàmhair, FE 27 — The weather-cairns of Cnoc ghlas
  • 13 an Giblean, FE 2,472 — The late snow on the high passes

Dùn dhearg

city · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 25,678

Founded 9 an Gearran, VE 9,597 by households who owed nothing to Dùn ìseal. Known for its red hill-fort.

Dùn dhearg is the red hill-fort city of the east and the seat of its province, a city of more than twenty-five thousand. The mills of Muileann dhomhain grind its bread and the quarries of Cnoc ghlas built its houses. It keeps the Old Spirits, and its old fort is the site of the province's ancestor feasts.

Muileann gheal

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 12,710

Founded 7 an Dàmhair, LE 1,082 by white-stone millers. Known for its flour for Dùn dhearg.

A white stone mill in the south-east that grinds for the city of Dùn dhearg. It keeps the Old Spirits and is a large mill-town with a guild of millers older than the city's walls.

  • 26 an Lùnastal, LE 1,439 — The grey glaze of Muileann gheal
  • 30 an Dùbhlachd, LE 1,509 — The grey glaze lost

Tobar ìseal

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,174

Founded 26 am Faoilleach, LE 508 by well-keepers of Dùn dhearg. Known for the well that waters Dùn dhearg.

A low well-village in the east that waters the city of Dùn dhearg in dry seasons. It keeps the Old Spirits, and its well-keepers still bless the water before it is carted up the hill.

Siorrachd Dùn ìseal

Baile naomh

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 3,008

Founded 1 an Gearran, FE 319 by custodians of the holy wells. Known for its holy wells of the vein country.

Baile naomh, the holy town, grew around wells in the vein country that the Holy Age custodians held sacred. The hot springs of Muileann ruadh lie to the west and the silver workings of Muileann chiar to the north-west. It is a small town of shrines and lodging houses, keeping the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits.

Cill dhìreach

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,922

Founded 6 am Màrt, FE 2,650 by druids of the schools for the silver-miners. Known for its miners' temple by the silver seam.

A temple village a short way from the silver seam at Muileann chiar, whose house of the druid schools has served the silver-miners since the seam was first worked. In the Age of Strangers its druids kept a record of the miners killed underground, one of the few such records to survive. It is not the Cill dhìreach of the central country.

Cnoc àrsaidh

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,625

Founded 5 an t-Sultain, FE 777 by shepherds of the eastern hills. Known for its cairn hill and its shepherds.

Cnoc àrsaidh of Dùn ìseal is a hill town crowned by old cairns, above Baile naomh. It has been a shepherding place since the Holy Age. Its people keep the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits and tend the cairns at the turning of the seasons.

Cnoc òg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 9,720

Founded 7 an t-Iuchar, AE 80 by silver miners of Muileann chiar. Known for the citadel over the silver seam.

A young hill-town with a citadel beside the silver mine of Muileann chiar, raised when the Ròdaich held the silver seam against the human claims. The citadel was built to guard the seam, and the town grew as the silver town grew. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Dùn ìseal

city · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 22,571

Founded 9 an Lùnastal, VE 5,324 by the hill-folk of the first Stone King. Known for the Hall of Brìde's flame.

A low fort-city in the east with walls, a citadel and a temple, the seat of Siorrachd Dùn ìseal. Its temple is the Hall where Brìde's undying flame was first bound, kept by the Ròdaich custodians through every age; the townsfolk themselves keep the Old Spirits, and their ancestor hall beside it is the chief spirit-house of the eastern hills. It stands between the silver seam of Muileann chiar and the hot springs of Muileann ruadh, and it was held by the Ròdaich in the dispute over the silver. It is the market town of the eastern hills and plain, and the market under the Hall is older than the kingdom. The silver, gold and copper of its hills pass through it as blanks for the mint, and the town salts venison and binds books.

Muileann chiar

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,771

Founded 10 an Lùnastal, FE 7 by Ròdaich custodians who found the silver seam. Known for the island's silver seam.

Muileann chiar was founded when a seam of silver was found near the great vein but not of it, the first wealth proved in the island's rock that was not the black glass. In the Age of Strangers the humans' concerns tried to claim the silver too, and the Ròdaich kept it; the town grew beside the obsidian workings as the call for both rose. It is smaller now than in its great years.

Muileann dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 8,100

Founded 23 am Màrt, FE 2,637 by Ròdaich millers of Dùn ìseal. Known for its deep-cut mill-race.

The deep mill takes its name from a mill-race cut far down into the rock to reach a steady flow. It grinds for Dùn dhearg and the villages around it and has done so since the Holy Age. The Old Spirits, the old rite of the ancestors, hold here, and each new millstone is blessed at the hearth before it is set.

Muileann ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,558

Founded 11 an t-Ògmhios, FE 405 by keepers of the hot springs. Known for the hot springs of Muileann ruadh.

A red walled mill town beside Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh, the hot springs whose warm water drives its wheel through winter. The keepers of the Old Spirits held the springs sacred, and the healers of the Old Faith call them Dian Cècht's. The town walled them against the claims of the human administration. It is a place for the sick and the old to bathe.

Siorrachd Dùn thais

Àth chaol

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,837

Founded 12 an Lùnastal, LE 1,401 by carters of Dùn thais. Known for its narrow ford on the Dùn thais road.

A small town at a narrow ford on the Dùn thais road, living on the carts that pass through it. Since the library was founded at Muileann chaol many of its young people have gone to work there as porters and copyists. It has never been walled or fought over.

Àth dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 11,388

Founded 6 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,930 by Ròdaich ford-keepers of Dùn thais. Known for its deep ford below Muileann chaol.

The deep ford lies below Muileann chaol, and every reader bound for the library crosses it. It is a town of eleven thousand. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Baile leathan

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,418

Founded 21 am Faoilleach, FE 2,093 by Ròdaich scribes of Dùn thais. Known for its copyists and binders for the library.

Baile leathan is one of the towns nearest Leabharlann Muileann chaol, and many of its people are copyists, binders and parchment-makers for the library. It was a market town of the broad valley long before the library was founded, and it grew quickly after. It keeps the druid schools' habit of reading aloud in the evenings.

Dùn thais

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 34,173

Founded 28 am Màrt, VE 7,796 by hill-folk pushing east. Known for its place as the great hill city near the Library.

Dùn thais of the north-east is a great hill city with a citadel and a temple, the chief place of its province. It lies close to Leabharlann Muileann chaol, and many of the Library's clerks and copyists live in it. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith, and its temple is sacred to Flidais, lady of the deer. Its tailors and smiths work for the library's clerks and the hill towns, and its own woods give timber.

Muileann àrsaidh

fort · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,831

Founded 19 am Faoilleach, FE 1,670 by a custodian house of Dùn thais. Known for its fortified ancient mill.

Muileann àrsaidh is an ancient mill fortified with a citadel, a short way from Muileann chaol. The citadel guarded the road to the ore in the Holy Age and now guards the road to the library. It is a small place of fewer than two thousand.

Siorrachd Inis bhàn

Doire ruadh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 4,987

Founded 24 an Cèitean, LE 1,491 by hawk-keepers of the north. Known for its red oak grove and hawk-keepers.

Doire ruadh is a village of red oaks inland of the Hawk bay, founded in the long quiet centuries by families who kept hawks for the rite of Mòd, the hungry hawk of Acaill. Its birds are still flown at the Hawk order's gatherings in Cnoc bheag. Since the Severance it has lain close to the Tuathaich border and has seen more soldiers than it wishes.

Inis bhàn

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 37,990

Founded 16 an Giblean, VE 9,239 by seal-taking households of the lower river. Known for its white-island river port and Hawk-order shrines.

Inis bhàn is the great river port of the north-west Ròdaich country and the seat of its province, a town of nearly forty thousand on the Abhainn ìseal whose barges run down to Ros gheal on the coast. It is a town of the Hawk order, and its shrines face down the river toward the sea. The Green Death, A' Phlàigh Uaine, struck it in the Age of Strangers. It is one of several towns that claim the dock from which the ships of the Sundering set out, a claim the others dispute and no roll can settle.

Siorrachd Inis bheag

Achadh gharbh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 9,900

Founded 7 an Dàmhair, LE 205 by farmers from Inis bheag. Known for its stony fields that feed Inis bheag.

Rough ground behind the river port of Inis bheag, broken to the plough in the long centuries after the Sundering fleet had gone. It feeds the river port and its fishing boats, and it has grown larger than many towns while keeping the name and customs of a village. The druid schools have a strong following among its farmers, who are said to argue the schools' questions over the furrow.

Achadh gharbh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,679

Founded 3 am Faoilleach, LE 1,104 by farmers of Muileann chaol. Known for its stony fields for the old mill.

A rough field village beside the older Muileann chaol, breaking stony ground for the mill. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and shares its name with two other Achadh gharbhs of the east, which the library's clerks tell apart only by their shires.

Inis bheag

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 21,240

Founded 25 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,435 by boat-builders of the north-east. Known for its boatyards of the small isle.

Inis bheag is an island town on the Abhainn bheag in the north-east and the seat of its province. Its boatyards have built fishing craft for the coast since the Holy Age and send them down the river to the sea at Caol chrom. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and shares its river with Ros fhionn of the old bridge.

  • 29 an Dàmhair, AE 53 — Ore through Inis bheag
  • 11 an Cèitean, SE 19 — The chest from Inis bheag

Muileann dhearg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,708

Founded 15 an Giblean, LE 1,566 by red-stone millers. Known for its red mill beside Muileann fhada.

A red mill town beside Muileann fhada in the north-east, the two together grinding for Doire chiar. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Ros fhionn

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,812

Founded 29 an Lùnastal, FE 41 by custodians of the river crossing. Known for Drochaid Ros fhionn, the old bridge.

Ros fhionn of Inis bheag is a walled city on a headland over the Abhainn bheag, founded in the Holy Age where the first bridges crossed the river. Drochaid Ros fhionn, the old crossing, is still standing. Little has crossed it since the salt went by sea, save in the century when the Company's ore carts used it on the eastern ore road; it fell silent again when the eastern pits flooded in the Severance war. The salt-boats' lane round the east cape, Seòlaid Ros fhionn, is named for the town. Its temple is a hall of the druid schools, sacred to Flidais. The salt trade that built the bridge is gone, but the market-court the salt-masters set up stayed on the headland. The town is still the market of fifty-three towns of the north-eastern hills, and no market on the island reaches further. Its yards on the river build barges and hulls, and it makes cheese for the hill towns.

Tobar òg

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 6,303

Founded 21 an t-Iuchar, LE 1,395 by well-diggers of Inis bheag. Known for the young well behind Inis bheag.

A young well village in the north-east, dug to water the fields behind Inis bheag when those fields were first broken. It has grown into a sizeable village and follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Siorrachd Inis chrom

Baile shean

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,839

Founded 18 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,185 by road-guards of Caol leathan. Known for its old walls and its house of the Stone.

An old walled town of Òrd na Cloiche, the order of the Stone, beside the fort of Muileann bheag. Its walls are older than the fort, and for most of its history it was the stronger of the two. It is small now, and lives on the fort's custom.

Cnoc shean

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,784

Founded 19 an Dùbhlachd, FE 202 by the lords of the old hill. Known for the old hill citadel.

A small old hill-town with a citadel in the west, commanding the road between Baile Mòr fhionn and the harbours of the south-west. It follows the order of the Stone and has kept a garrison since the war before the Severance.

Inis chrom

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 31,994

Founded 25 an Giblean, FE 1,601 by sailors of the south-west. Known for its bent isle harbour and its sailors of the Stone.

Inis chrom is a large walled harbour on a bent island in the mouth of the Abhainn ghorm in the south-west. It has been a port since the Holy Age and its sailors keep the order of the Stone. It lies close to Am Buabhall Fortanach and Àth gharbh.

Siorrachd Inis mhin

Baile ruadh

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 11,186

Founded 9 an t-Iuchar, FE 957 by Ròdaich farmers of the red ground. Known for a shared market on the border.

A red town in the north-west that stayed Ròdaich when the Tuathaich homeland was fixed around it, and the line of the border wall that was proposed and never built would have run past its gate. It keeps the Old Spirits of the Ròdaich, and its market is used by Tuathaich from Baile fhionn and Ròdaich from Àth uaine alike.

Inis mhin

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 12,779

Founded 5 an Lùnastal, FE 2,644 by Ròdaich harbour-folk; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the telling of Naomh Breandan's voyage in its Tuathaich port.

Inis mhin was a Ròdaich harbour of the Holy Age on a tidal islet of the north coast, and its citadel was raised in the Age of Strangers by human administrators guarding the northern landing. After the Severance it passed wholly to the Tuathaich, and it is now one of their chief ports. It is among the coastal towns where the voyage of Naomh Breandan is still told, and its church keeps the old Tuathaich telling more closely than the churches of its neighbours. In the first spring of the Severance war the Leaden Hawk company, Buidheann an t-Seabhaig Luaidhe, lay twelve hours in the town and heard of the constables riding the western roads.

Siorrachd Inis mhòr

Cnoc naomh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 7,832

Founded 29 an Cèitean, FE 1,142 by a custodian house of Inis mhòr. Known for its citadel on the holy hill.

The holy hill carried a shrine before it carried a citadel; the citadel was added to guard Inis mhòr from the hills. The shrine still stands inside the walls. The fourth regiment from Caol bheag drills on the plain below it. On the moor above the town is Coinneachadh a' Mhonaidh, the cairn where the crew-leaders of the northern pits fixed the week of their rising.

Inis mhòr

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 23,990

Founded 16 an Dàmhair, VE 9,651 by net-fishers of the Abhainn ghorm. Known for its north-eastern river fleet and debating halls.

Inis mhòr of the north-east is the great river port of its province, on the Abhainn ghorm, a fishing town of the Ancient Age that the trade of the Age of Strangers made a city; its barges run down the river to Ros chiar at the mouth. Its people follow the druid schools of the Old Faith, and the town's debating halls were among the first to reopen at the schools' revival. It shares the river and coastal trade with Ceann bheag and the walled town of Baile Mòr dhìreach inland.

Siorrachd Inis thais

Àth ghlas

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 16,521

Founded 31 am Faoilleach, FE 1,413 by Ròdaich traders of Inis thais. Known for its grey ford market of the west.

Àth ghlas is a large ford-market of the west, near Seann Warr. It follows the order of Manannan. It is one of three places named Àth ghlas and the largest.

Baile dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,014

Founded 14 an t-Iuchar, LE 1,392 by traders of the order of Manannan from the west. Known for its straight-street harbour of the order of Manannan.

Baile dhìreach, the straight town, is a harbour on the west coast built around one long street to the quay. It was founded in the long quiet centuries by traders of the order of Manannan, among neighbours of the order of the Stone. The two orders have shared its market without any trouble the rolls have thought fit to set down.

Caol fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 11,425

Founded 13 an t-Iuchar, LE 739 by fishers of the wild strait. Known for its fishing in the wild strait.

Caol fhiadhaich is a harbour on a rough strait of the west coast, within the province of Inis thais. It was founded in the long quiet centuries by fishers who braved waters the older harbours avoided. Its people keep the Old Faith in the order of the Stone. Its women distil scent-waters, the town's second trade after the fishing. The southern sea-lane, Slighe-mhara Caol fhiadhaich, is named for its fishers, who first sailed it round the south coast in the long quiet centuries.

Inis thais

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 34,904

Founded 21 an Lùnastal, VE 7,731 by Ròdaich fishing households of the western coast. Known for the temple of Lia Fàil and its pilgrims.

Inis thais is a walled temple city of the south-west and the seat of its province. Its temple of Lia Fàil, the stone called Clach that cries out under the rightful king, is the chief house of the order of the Stone, and pilgrims come to it from Caol leathan and the whole western coast. It has been a holy city since the Holy Age. Besides its pilgrims it lives on its shipyard, which builds seagoing hulls for the western coast, and on its cheese and books. Buidheann an t-Seabhaig Luaidhe, the Leaden Hawk company sent by the council in the Severance war, ended its road at the temple here; the druids of Lia Fàil kept the city out of the war but shut its harbour to the Company's ships.

Siorrachd Muileann àrsaidh

Achadh àrsaidh

village · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 1,756

Founded 14 am Màrt, FE 603 by Ròdaich fishers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the watch for the Sea-Watcher.

An ancient field village on the far western coast, facing the waters of Uilebheist na Mara, the Sea-Watcher. Gorta Baile chrom, the Great Hunger, struck it in the Age of Strangers; it was resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance and keeps the faith of the Church. Pirates have been seen offshore and the villagers keep watch on the headland. Its boats first met the humans' ships at sea, off the north-west cape at the place they call Coinneachadh nan Long.

Achadh fhiadhaich

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,753

Founded 19 an t-Iuchar, LE 1,512 by Ròdaich fishers of the west coast. Known for its fishing within sight of the Sea-Watcher's waters.

A wild field village on the far western shore with a small harbour, kept in Ròdaich hands when the Tuathaich homeland was fixed to the north. It faces the waters where the Sea-Watcher is said to live, and pirates are still seen off the coast. Its people follow the order of Manannan.

Cathair gheal

city · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 9,818

Founded 5 am Màrt, VE 6,701 by builders of the western coast; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for its white walls against the pirate coast.

Cathair gheal is a walled city of white stone on the far western coast, built by the Ròdaich and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Its walls face the sea, where pirate ships have been seen offshore. It is the market for the Tuathaich villages of Muileann àrsaidh province. Its smiths make the tools of the north-west.

  • 28 an Cèitean, AE 50 — Cathair gheal in the northern concession
  • 24 an Cèitean, AE 150 — Cathair gheal behind its walls

Cnoc bhàn

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 6,480

Founded 30 an Dùbhlachd, LE 62 by Ròdaich fishers; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for its harbour facing the pirate waters.

Cnoc bhàn of the north-west is a harbour facing the pirate waters. It was founded by Ròdaich fishers in the long quiet centuries and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Its boats avoid the waters where old sailors place the Sea-Watcher.

Cnoc gheal

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 1,883

Founded 16 an Cèitean, LE 555 by Ròdaich shepherds; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for its white hill sheepfolds on the line.

A white hill of sheepfolds, Ròdaich until the Severance and Tuathaich since. The Ròdaich Cnoc gheal lies a short walk south-west, over the line. The two villages share a name and very little else: the one has its church, the other its shrine of Manannan.

Cnoc uaine

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 6,864

Founded 9 an Dàmhair, LE 938 by Ròdaich herders; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for its green hill grazing.

Cnoc uaine of Muileann àrsaidh is a green hill of the north-west, founded by Ròdaich herders in the long quiet centuries. It was resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It is a grazing town and keeps the faith of the Church.

Muileann àrsaidh

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 1,643

Founded 10 an t-Iuchar, FE 2,444 by Ròdaich millers; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the old mill of the north-west.

Muileann àrsaidh, the ancient mill, is the younger of the two Muileann àrsaidh in the Tuathaich north-west, founded as a Ròdaich mill town in the Holy Age; the seat of the shire is the elder town close by. It was walled in the Age of Strangers and resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. The mill still grinds for the surrounding villages.

  • 28 an Cèitean, AE 150 — Muileann àrsaidh closes its road

Muileann àrsaidh

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 12,968

Founded 3 an t-Samhain, VE 7,789 by Ròdaich millers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the elder of the two ancient mills.

An ancient mill town of the north-west, and seat of Siorrachd Muileann àrsaidh, resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. A second Muileann àrsaidh lies close by, and the two are called the elder and the younger. It follows the faith of the Church.

Muileann leathan

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 3,096

Founded 23 an Lùnastal, SE 13 by Tuathaich millers. Known for its Tuathaich grain mill.

Muileann leathan of the north-west was built by Tuathaich settlers soon after the Severance to grind grain for the northern villages, which had lost the Ròdaich mills to the south. It is a small town, and its mill-race was dug by hand by the first households. It keeps the faith of the Church. Amber washed up on the nearby shore is its other trade.

Seann Skell

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 2,400

Founded 10 an Gearran, VE 1,389 by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for its watch over the pirate waters.

Seann Skell is a Seann-Dhaoine harbour on the far north-west coast, named by the Ròdaich who resettled it; it passed to the Tuathaich after the Severance. Its citadel looks out over the waters where pirate ships are still reported and where old sailors place the Sea-Watcher. It is not the Seann Skell whose name the regiments carry, which lies far to the south-east.

  • 10 an Dùbhlachd, VE 1,807 — The tower at the north-western Seann Skell

Tobar dhearg

village · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 4,154

Founded 16 an Dùbhlachd, FE 1,150 by Ròdaich well-keepers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for its red well of the western Tuathaich.

A Ròdaich village around a well of red water, resettled by Tuathaich families after the Severance. Like several villages of this coast it made the shrine of Manannan that it inherited its church rather than raising its own. It lives on sheep and on the market at Cathair gheal.

  • 30 am Faoilleach, DE 17 — Tobar dhearg of the hills

Siorrachd Muileann bhàn

Cnoc mhòr

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 8,008

Founded 31 an Cèitean, LE 1,645 by hill-lords of Muileann bhàn. Known for its hill-farms above Seann Warr.

A great hill in the south, above the harbour of Seann Warr and the large mill town of Muileann bhàn. It keeps the Old Spirits, and its hill-farms supply both.

Doire dhearg

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 1,668

Founded 21 an t-Iuchar, AE 32 by Ròdaich miners bound by the strangers' contracts. Known for its red spoil-heaps of the camp years.

Doire dhearg began as a mining camp in the Age of Strangers, when the interior was first worked by the ton. Its red spoil-heaps are still visible above the village. Many of its people left when the workings moved on, and the village that remains keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits.

Muileann bhàn

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 34,517

Founded 24 an Dàmhair, VE 7,701 by herders of the eastern plain. Known for its white mills and citadel of the ore road.

Muileann bhàn is a town of thirty-four thousand with a citadel, the seat of its province, standing where the ore road from the eastern diggings met the mills. In the Age of Strangers its citadel held the human administration's weighing-house and its guards. The mills have turned to grain since the Severance, and the Old Spirits, the old rite of the ancestors, which were never lost here, have come back to the square.

Siorrachd Muileann bheag

Àth gheal

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 9,316

Founded 20 an t-Ògmhios, LE 1,021 by farmers of Muileann bheag. Known for its white ford near Seann Tarr.

Àth gheal of Muileann bheag is a ford town near Seann Tarr, founded in the long quiet centuries. It keeps the ancestor rite of the Old Spirits. At the great feasts it lodges the pilgrims bound for the shrine at Seann Tarr.

Baile bheag

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,897

Founded 3 an t-Samhain, LE 1,046 by toll-keepers of Muileann bheag. Known for a walled town of tolls.

A small town on the road to Muileann bheag, walled to collect tolls rather than to keep enemies out. It still collects them, and has outlived every attempt to take the right away. It is one of several places named Baile bheag.

Cill àrsaidh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 11,868

Founded 25 an t-Sultain, FE 2,924 by keepers of the Old Spirits. Known for a druids' house on an old shrine.

An ancient cell-site village in the north-east, older than the druid schools that now hold it. The founding shrine is said to have been of the Old Spirits, and its foundations lie under the present meeting-house. It is a large village supplying Muileann bheag.

Doire uaine

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 6,576

Founded 16 an Lùnastal, FE 1,738 by the grove-keepers of the Old Spirits. Known for its oak for Muileann bheag.

A green oak grove in the north-east, not the Doire uaine of the Hollow Man's hills, a confusion the library records note with some weariness. It keeps the Old Spirits and cuts its oak for Muileann bheag.

Dùn dhubh

city · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,841

Founded 26 an Cèitean, FE 1,182 by a custodian house of Muileann bheag. Known for its black fort over the coast road.

Dùn dhubh is a walled hill fort of dark stone, ranked a city though it holds under three thousand people. It commands the coast road above Muileann bheag and the harbour of Seann Toll. Its walls were raised in the Holy Age and repaired in every age after. A dubhan works stands under its walls, on the old charcoal-burners' ground.

Muileann bheag

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 11,908

Founded 23 an Giblean, FE 1,789 by grain-millers of the north-east. Known for its flour for the north-east harbours.

A small mill that grew into a sizable town and the seat of Siorrachd Muileann bheag. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and grinds for the harbour at Ros chiar. It shares its name with three others on the island, including the Tuathaich lighthouse town.

  • 27 am Màrt, AE 143 — Muileann bheag in the north-east

Ros chiar

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,817

Founded 19 an Lùnastal, LE 1,488 by fishers of Muileann bheag. Known for the flour harbour of Muileann bheag.

A dusky headland harbour village on the north-east coast that ships the flour of Muileann bheag. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith and competes with Seann Toll for the coast trade.

Seann Tarr

city · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 3,806

Founded 30 an Cèitean, VE 2 by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for its north-eastern ancestor shrine.

Seann Tarr is a Seann-Dhaoine site on the north-eastern coast, resettled by the Ròdaich in the Holy Age, and its ancestor hall is one of the oldest spirit-houses of the Old Spirits still in use. A citadel was raised over the harbour in the Age of Sundering. It is small for a city, but the shrine draws the whole north-east at the great feasts. It is the market town of the north-eastern coast, whose market began at the shrine's feasts. Honey from its heather and wax for the shrine lights are its own goods, with cheese and books, and its rope-makers are a chartered guild.

Seann Toll

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,603

Founded 19 an Giblean, VE 2,319 by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for its cleft-rock harbour of the Old Ones.

Seann Toll is a harbour in a cleft of the rock, and its lowest quay is cut in a manner the Ròdaich did not use; it is held to be the work of the Seann-Dhaoine, and nothing more is known of it. The Ròdaich settled it in the Holy Age as the nearest harbour for Dùn dhubh and Muileann bheag. It is a small port town of fishers and lightermen.

Siorrachd Muileann chiar

Àth chaol

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,790

Founded 30 an Dùbhlachd, AE 66 by miners of the central diggings. Known for its miners, who died in the Rending.

A narrow ford-town in the central hills, grown in the Age of Strangers around the camp-roads to the diggings near Cill ghlas. The Rending, Scàineadh Cill ghlas, killed miners of this town in the collapse, and the people here still use scàinte of a man who is shaken. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Àth dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,056

Founded 20 an Giblean, FE 2,404 by carriers of the mountain country. Known for its straight ford of the ore carts.

Àth dhìreach, high in the mountain country, was a carriers' settlement of the Holy Age that the shared-meal law fed through the poor season, and in the Age of Strangers the ore carts crossed at its ford. It is a town of three thousand in the eastern mining district. Its ford is paved with spoil from the diggings.

  • 18 an Dàmhair, FE 2,474 — Àth dhìreach after the poor season

Doire uaine

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,599

Founded 13 an Gearran, FE 2,879 by herders of the Doire uaine hills. Known for the Hollow Man of the hills.

Doire uaine is a small village in the hills where inscriptions describe the Hollow Man, something that walked without breathing and attacked anyone who lit a fire in its sight. The village was founded in the Holy Age. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

  • 8 an Cèitean, VE 3,196 — Signs cut in the Doire uaine hills

Muileann chiar

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 15,578

Founded 23 an t-Iuchar, LE 365 by ore-crushers of the eastern diggings. Known for its ore mills of the eastern district.

Muileann chiar, seat of the province of the same name, began as an ore-crushing mill for the diggings in the hills east of the capital. It grew large in the Age of Strangers, when the district was worked by the ton, and lost its trade when Scàineadh Cill ghlas, a short way west, closed the district for a generation. It is not the silver town of the same name further east, and the two are often confused in the older records.

Muileann gheal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 688

Founded 20 an Lùnastal, FE 2,347 by mountain households of the carriers' country. Known for its walled mill-camp under Doire uaine.

Muileann gheal was a mountain settlement of the Holy Age whose common granary was opened in the poor season, and in the Age of Strangers it was walled as a mill-camp under the Doire uaine hills to crush ore from the eastern diggings. It is small, fewer than seven hundred people. The warm springs of Muileann ruadh lie a short walk away, and the camp's miners bathed there.

Siorrachd Muileann chrom

Achadh dhomhain

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 14,105

Founded 10 an t-Ògmhios, FE 272 by farmers of Muileann chrom. Known for its deep-field granaries of the camps.

Achadh dhomhain of Muileann chrom is a large farming village in deep fields, founded in the Holy Age. Its granaries fed the mining camps in the Age of Strangers and were requisitioned in the war of the Severance. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Àth ìseal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,979

Founded 7 an t-Iuchar, LE 324 by Ròdaich ferrymen of Muileann chrom. Known for the low ford and its ferry.

The low ford floods each wet season, and for part of every year the crossing is made by ferry. The town is small and has always been poor. It sends its surplus down to the quays at Inis ìseal and Ceann fhada.

Baile dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,666

Founded 10 am Faoilleach, AE 34 by a Company surveyor, as a camp for the pits. Known for its tithe-fields of the Cnoc bhàn druids.

Baile dhomhain was laid out on a grid by a Company surveyor in the Age of Strangers, a camp for the deep workings and the first town of the Ròdaich drawn on paper before a stone of it was set; two of its streets were pulled down for a spoil-tip before the Severance. It is a small town in a deep valley now, farming for the house of Macha's order at Cnoc bhàn, whose tithe-rolls record its harvests without a gap since the kingdom was restored.

  • 10 am Faoilleach, AE 34 — Baile dhomhain raised as a camp town

Ceann fhada

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 6,509

Founded 27 an Cèitean, LE 1,359 by Ròdaich river pilots. Known for its long quay and river pilots.

A long spit of land made Ceann fhada a landing for river craft, and its pilots have guided boats on the Abhainn uaine for centuries. It is the old rival of Inis ìseal, a short way downstream, and the two quays have quarrelled over tolls in every age the rolls cover. It prospered in the Age of Strangers carrying ore-cart loads by water and has held its trade since by carrying grain.

  • 23 an t-Iuchar, AE 12 — An ore quay at Ceann fhada
  • 24 an Cèitean, AE 149 — The quay at Ceann fhada seized

Cnoc fhiadhaich

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,965

Founded 17 am Màrt, LE 488 by hunters of the Muileann chrom country. Known for a walled hill by the river road.

A wild walled hill in the middle country, near the canoe-landing of Cidhe Beag on Abhainn uaine. Its walls were raised in the troubled years when the river road carried ore. It follows the order of Macha and trades with Muileann chrom and Inis ìseal.

Cuan dhearg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 3,135

Founded 12 an Dàmhair, LE 1,789 by river fishers of the Abhainn uaine. Known for its red-cliffed river landing and ferries.

Cuan dhearg is one of the ring of small river towns on the Abhainn uaine above Cathair mhòr, named for the red cliffs over its landing. It lives on the river fish and the short ferry runs between the river towns, and sends what it has for the sea down to Ceann leathan at the river mouth. It has never been walled. It is not the southern Cuan dhearg that Tonn Mhòr destroyed; the chroniclers have confused the two more than once. Its inn, An Cupa Dàna, is where Buidheann an t-Seabhaig Luaidhe, the Leaden Hawk company, gathered in the first spring of the Severance war before walking to the Hawk coast.

  • 17 an Giblean, AE 150 — The Leaden Hawk company

Doire mhòr

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,738

Founded 24 an Giblean, LE 568 by Ròdaich hill households above Muileann chrom. Known for its refusal of the first contract.

Doire mhòr, the great oak grove, was a hill village above Muileann chrom when the humans came, and the first settlement to refuse the Company's contract: its custodian Beathag Dhubh told the agent that the hill was not hers to sell. The Company turned its stream to wash ore, and at last took the village itself for a shaft beneath the hill, and its last households were carried out by constables. The beacon of the day the pits stopped was lit on its hill. The oak wood went long ago to pit-props, and a few families farm the clearing.

Inis ìseal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,887

Founded 12 an Giblean, LE 1,110 by Ròdaich river boatmen. Known for its river-island port on the Abhainn uaine.

Inis ìseal is a river port on a low island in the Abhainn uaine, a short way from the landing at Cidhe Beag. It is the rival of Ceann fhada a short way upstream, and the two have disputed tolls in every age. It prospered in the Age of Strangers carrying ore and has kept its trade by carrying grain.

Muileann chrom

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 18,448

Founded 11 an Gearran, FE 1,556 by Ròdaich millers on the river bend. Known for the great mill on the river bend.

The mill on the bend of the river gave its name to the town and then to the province, of which it is the seat and the largest place. It ground grain for the whole central country and, in the Age of Strangers, for the camps east of it as well. It is a busy town and has never needed walls, standing between Cathair mhòr and Ceann leathan on the road that joins them. In the last years of the humans' rule the Company laid the ore line from its yards, and the railway ran from its pits by Cathair dhearg down to the quay at Ros dhomhain; the kingdom's Rail Board keeps its yards here still.

Muileann dhearg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,843

Founded 26 an Gearran, LE 797 by millers of Muileann chrom. Known for its walled red mill.

A walled mill town on the road north of Muileann chrom, one of three places named Muileann dhearg. It was walled in the Age of Strangers to protect its stores. It follows the capital's order, the order of Macha.

Seann Toll

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 8,455

Founded 8 an Gearran, VE 92 by the Seann-Dhaoine. Known for the rock-hollow landing and Còmhrag crowds.

A Seann-Dhaoine river port on the Abhainn uaine in the midlands, called Seann Toll by the Ròdaich for the hollow in the rock where its boats lie. It is walled and follows the order of Macha, and it stands a short way west of Cill ghlas, where the Rending opened. It lies close to Ceann leathan at the river mouth, where the Còmhrag is fought each year, and fighters from the tournament fill its taverns.

Siorrachd Muileann dhearg

Baile thais

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 13,140

Founded 5 an t-Ògmhios, FE 2,086 by river-boatmen of the Abhainn uaine. Known for the Cidhe Beag landing on the Abhainn uaine.

Baile thais stands on the Abhainn uaine where the river leaves the hills for its run down to the gulf, and the river landing of Cidhe Beag lies just downstream. Boats have been launched here since the Holy Age to carry goods inland and ore down. It is a busy, unwalled town of boatmen and warehouses. Slighe-mhara Caol fhiadhaich, the southern sea-lane, ends at the landing of Cidhe Beag below the town.

Cill fhada

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,783

Founded 17 an Dùbhlachd, LE 96 by wood-watchers of the western wood. Known for the long temple of Macha.

A temple-site village strung along a long ridge near Baile chrom, whose temple of Macha is the longest building in the district. It farms for the market at Baile chrom and sends its grain to the tithe-granaries there.

Cill ghlas

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,711

Founded 4 am Faoilleach, FE 1,814 by a house of the druid schools. Known for Scàineadh Cill ghlas, the Rending.

Cill ghlas, the grey cell, was a quiet village of the druid schools in the hills east of the capital until in the Age of Strangers the workings were driven under it. Late in that age a common cutting tore open a fault around the village; dozens were killed and the working was closed. From the Rending the island has the word 'scàinte'. The village was rebuilt on the far side of the crack, and its people still mark the day of the dead.

Cnoc chaol

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 655

Founded 22 an Cèitean, VE 7,727 by hill-folk of the vein country. Known for a spent camp on the narrow hill.

Cnoc chaol, on the narrow hill, was a hill settlement of the Ancient Age, where one of the first copies of the keeper's stone cup was ground, and in the Age of Strangers it was a mining camp worked by the ton. It emptied after Scàineadh Cill ghlas closed the district and never recovered. Fewer than seven hundred people live there now, among the spoil heaps.

Muileann dhearg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 22,453

Founded 2 an t-Ògmhios, FE 1,179 by Ròdaich millers of the central country. Known for its stamping mills turned to grain.

The red mill is the seat of its province and one of the largest towns of the centre, standing between Seann Chwen and Cnoc ghorm. Its mills stamped ore in the Age of Strangers and turned back to grain after the Severance. It is a town of the capital's order, the order of Macha, busy and unwalled.

Muileann dhearg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 14,052

Founded 30 an t-Sultain, LE 2 by ore-millers of the central diggings. Known for its red mill beside Cill ghlas.

Muileann dhearg, seat of its province, is a mill town a short way from Cill ghlas. Scàineadh Cill ghlas tore open the hills nearby and killed dozens, and the town's mills stood idle for a generation after. It follows the druid schools of the Old Faith.

Siorrachd Muileann dhomhain

Achadh chaol

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,691

Founded 5 an Dùbhlachd, AE 137 by the folk of the district closed after the Rending. Known for its narrow fields on the edge of the fenced ground.

Achadh chaol was built by the folk of the district the Company fenced and closed after Scàineadh Cill ghlas, the Rending. It stands on the edge of the fenced ground, on land the custodians of Muileann dhomhain lent them at Coinneachadh an Fhearainn, the standing stone on the moor road, and it is the only settlement of that age founded by Ròdaich for Ròdaich with no Company surveyor's hand in it. It is a village of narrow fields, and it sends its grain to the mills around it.

  • 5 an Dùbhlachd, AE 137 — Achadh chaol raised by the dispossessed

Achadh ìseal

village · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 2,104

Founded 27 an t-Sultain, LE 1,184 by farmers from Muileann dhomhain. Known for its harvests for the southern mills.

A low field village in the south-east, farming for the mill town of Muileann dhomhain and the port of Ceann chaol. It keeps the Old Spirits. Of its history nothing is written but its harvests.

Caol naomh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,711

Founded 17 an Giblean, LE 481 by druids of Òrd Bhrìde. Known for its pilgrim landing of Òrd Bhrìde.

A holy strait-harbour near the ruins of Làrach an Dùin-fhaire, where the orthodox order of Brìde's flame built a landing for pilgrims coming to the mountain of Crom's stone. It is one of the few towns where Òrd Bhrìde holds the majority, and its druids were among those who set down the order's rite in the first years of the new kingdom. It is a small town and quiet outside the pilgrim season. Pilgrims' boats from the southern Seann Skell come round to its landing by Slighe-mhara chritheanach, the shaking sea-way, named for the swell off the south cape.

Ceann chaol

city · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 9,536

Founded 23 an Giblean, FE 145 by Ròdaich seafarers of the narrow point. Known for its narrow-point harbour, rival of Ceann mhin.

Ceann chaol is a port city on the narrow point, and the old rival of Ceann mhin along the same shore. Its ships carry the flour of Muileann dhomhain and the grain of the eastern plain. The two harbours have disputed fishing grounds in every age, and the rolls of their disputes are long.

  • 4 am Màrt, FE 151 — The carriers' path to Ceann chaol
  • 20 an t-Samhain, AE 103 — The deep quay at Ceann chaol

Muileann dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 16,277

Founded 8 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,747 by the millers of the deep race. Known for the grain-exchange of the south-east.

A mill on a deep, fast race in the central country and the seat of Siorrachd Muileann dhomhain. It was a milling town for centuries and grew rich carrying grain to the mining settlements in the Age of Strangers, when the camps could no longer feed themselves. It keeps the Old Spirits of the Ròdaich, and its grain-exchange still sets the price of flour for the south-east.

Muileann dhomhain

town · Ròdaich · Na Seann Spioradan · pop. 20,506

Founded 9 an t-Samhain, FE 1,417 by Ròdaich millers of the south-east. Known for its deep mill-pools feeding Ceann chaol's ships.

Muileann dhomhain, seat of its province, is a town of twenty thousand built around deep mill-pools fed from the hills. Its flour goes down to the quays of Ceann chaol and out by sea, and the two towns have leaned on each other since the Holy Age. It is not the smaller Muileann dhomhain of Dùn ìseal to the north.

  • 29 an Lùnastal, LE 1,079 — The swallowing cough at Muileann dhomhain

Muileann uaine

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,705

Founded 8 am Màrt, AE 48 by a human milling concern with Ròdaich labour. Known for its ore-crushing mill of the interior workings.

Muileann uaine was built in the Age of Strangers as a crushing mill for ore from the interior workings. It is not the Muileann uaine of the Cnoc bheag country that the Green Death struck, though the two are often confused. It is a small town now and keeps the orthodox rite of Òrd Bhrìde.

Siorrachd Muileann leathan

Baile fhionn

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 1,628

Founded 31 an Dàmhair, LE 1,772 by Ròdaich farmers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for its trade across the line with Baile ruadh.

A small fair town in the north-west, resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. It follows the Tuathaich Church and trades across the line with the Ròdaich town of Baile ruadh.

Baile leathan

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 1,609

Founded 21 an t-Iuchar, AE 23 by human settlers from an Tìr Thall. Known for an old strangers' settlement of the north.

Baile leathan was built by human settlers in the Age of Strangers on the northern coast, one of the few places the strangers founded rather than took. After the Severance it became a Tuathaich town. It keeps the faith of the Church and its oldest families still count their descent from the Crossing.

Cill chaol

village · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 1,898

Founded 10 am Màrt, FE 2,014 by Ròdaich druids; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for a Tuathaich church in a Ròdaich chapel.

Cill chaol was a narrow Ròdaich chapel village near the northern coast, emptied at the Severance and taken by Tuathaich families. They made its chapel a church of the Tuathaich, and the Ròdaich carvings on its doorposts were left in place beside theirs. It is a small place near the lighthouse of Muileann bheag.

Cnoc leathan

fort · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 2,319

Founded 9 an t-Samhain, AE 14 by the human administration, as a coast fort. Known for its Tuathaich-held fort on the north coast.

Cnoc leathan was built by the human administration as a fort on the northern coast road, not far from the lighthouse at Muileann bheag. The Tuathaich have held it since the Severance and keep its citadel manned. Its small garrison follows the Tuathaich Church.

Muileann bheag

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 2,177

Founded 14 an Giblean, LE 1,530 by Ròdaich millers, resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for Taigh-solais Muileann bheag.

A small mill town on the north coast beside Taigh-solais Muileann bheag, one of the five lighthouses built in the Age of Strangers. It became Tuathaich at the Severance, and the Tuathaich lighthouse-keepers tended the beacon for the kingdom until it was converted to dubhan. It follows the Tuathaich Church.

  • 13 am Faoilleach, AE 64 — The fishermen of Muileann bheag

Muileann leathan

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 22,366

Founded 24 an Giblean, VE 6,933 by weaving households of the north; resettled by the Tuathaich. Known for the Tuathaich mill-citadel.

A wide mill on a northern stream, walled with a citadel, and the seat of Siorrachd Muileann leathan. It was a Ròdaich town until the Severance, when the Tuathaich took it over as one of the principal towns of their homeland. It is a centre of the Tuathaich Church, and its keep is where the Tuathaich northern coast is governed.

Siorrachd Muileann mhin

Doire bheag

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 693

Founded 4 an t-Samhain, LE 1,560 by Ròdaich woodcutters of the capital. Known for its firewood for the capital.

A small village in an oak copse north-east of Cathair dhearg, which has cut firewood and charcoal for the capital for as long as there are accounts. It has never grown past seven hundred people. Its people follow the capital's order, the order of Macha, and take their wood into the city on market days.

Muileann mhin

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 30,105

Founded 20 an t-Iuchar, FE 1,458 by millers of the capital country. Known for the capital's flour mills.

Muileann mhin is a large river town on the Abhainn fhionn east of the capital and the seat of its province. Its flour mills have fed the capital since the Holy Age. It keeps the capital's order, the order of Macha, and ships its flour down the river to Cathair dhomhain and along the shore to Cathair dhearg and Ros dhomhain.

Siorrachd Muileann naomh

Àth chrom

town · Tuathaich · An Eaglais · pop. 2,343

Founded 3 an t-Iuchar, LE 989 by Ròdaich drovers; resettled by the Tuathaich after the Severance. Known for its Tuathaich drovers at the bent ford.

A drovers' town at the bent ford, Ròdaich until the Severance and Tuathaich since. It lies a short way from the field of Àth leathan, and its people carried the dead from that battle. It follows the faith of the Church.

  • 30 an t-Samhain, AE 150 — The columns at Àth chrom

Baile dhìreach

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,961

Founded 3 an Gearran, LE 1,075 by Ròdaich traders of Muileann naomh. Known for its straight street, the twin of Cnoc gheal's.

A small town of one straight street on the far west, twinned with Cnoc gheal a short walk away. It lies close to the Tuathaich line and trades with the villages beyond it. It follows the order of Manannan.

Caol ruadh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 11,899

Founded 14 an Giblean, VE 7,893 by Ròdaich fishers of the red strait. Known for its red strait and the orthodox rite of Brìde's flame.

Caol ruadh takes its name from the red rock of the strait it watches on the southern coast. It was a quiet fishing town for most of its history, and was among the first to take up the orthodox rite of Brìde's flame and Crom's stone when Òrd Bhrìde was first ordered. Since An Cogadh Fada its harbour has victualled the garrisons and the fleet at Seann Skell close by, and after that war it was chartered for the purpose as the sixteenth market town.

  • 14 an Giblean, VE 7,893 — Caol ruadh on the southern strait
  • 26 am Faoilleach, DE 23 — The market charter of Caol ruadh

Cill gharbh

village · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,948

Founded 27 an Lùnastal, FE 1,926 by Ròdaich druids of the western coast. Known for its rough stone shrine of the west.

A village around a rough stone shrine on the far western coast of the Ròdaich country. Its shrine is older than any of its houses, and Manannan was worshipped there before the orders divided. It is a small village of fewer than two thousand.

Cnoc dhearg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 1,714

Founded 31 an Lùnastal, LE 644 by potters of the west. Known for its red-clay potteries of the west.

Cnoc dhearg of Muileann naomh is a small town of the west, founded in the long quiet centuries on a hill of red clay. Its potteries supply jars and tiles to the western harbours, and the Age of Strangers brought it a brief trade in crucibles for the assayers. It keeps the order of Manannan.

Cnoc gheal

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 2,713

Founded 16 am Màrt, LE 784 by Ròdaich druids of the order of Manannan. Known for its white hill shrine of Manannan.

The Ròdaich Cnoc gheal is a white hill with a shrine of Manannan mac Lir, twinned with Baile dhìreach. A second Cnoc gheal, held by the Tuathaich, lies a short walk north-east over the line. The two villages share a name and very little else, not even a faith.

Cnoc òg

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 752

Founded 31 am Faoilleach, SE 2 by the restored kingdom, as a border post. Known for its border walls facing the Tuathaich.

Cnoc òg, "the young hill", was walled by the restored kingdom soon after the Severance, on the Ròdaich side of the line facing the Tuathaich towns to the north and west. It has never been more than a small town of soldiers' families and carters. In An Cogadh Fada it lay a short march behind the field at Àth leathan, and its walls held the wounded after that first battle.

Muileann naomh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 10,137

Founded 4 an t-Ògmhios, FE 599 by Ròdaich millers of the west coast. Known for the consecrated mill-wheel.

A holy mill in the west, the seat of Siorrachd Muileann naomh, whose wheel is said to have been consecrated to Manannan mac Lir. It lies near the Àth leathan battlefield and was taken over by crown regiments in the Long War. It follows the order of Manannan.

  • 6 an Dùbhlachd, AE 89 — Muileann naomh buys its way out

Muileann naomh

town · Ròdaich · An Creideamh Sean · pop. 12,401

Founded 24 am Faoilleach, VE 8,309 by Ròdaich households of the south coast. Known for its grain blessed by the druids of Brìde's flame.

A holy mill in the south, the seat of Siorrachd Muileann naomh, whose druids of the orthodox order of Brìde's flame bless the grain before it is ground. It is one of the few towns of Òrd Bhrìde and trades with Caol ruadh and Seann Skell. Its hawk-house was the southernmost of Òrd an t-Seabhaig, the first on Rodos to hang a bronze bell, until it took Òrd Bhrìde's written order in the first years of the restored kingdom; the bell now rings for Brìde's flame.
